5100b2e Merge pull request #37 from softwarewrighter/pr/local-blue-logo
# CoSy subset on reva-fork

A working subset of CoSy (`../sample/CoSy`) on the reva-fork portable core:
`CoSy.f` loads to the end with no errors, restores Bob's `CoSy.csy` into the
`R` dictionary and runs the `script0` stored in it. Vectors, reduce, strings,
nested lists, floats and `R` work at the REPL, and `save` writes `R` back.

Needs reva-fork `dev` with the vx86 `a0`–`a3` fix (PR #12; without it loading
stops in `Furniture.f` with `unsupported instruction ... a3`) and the x87
floats of PR #21, which `needs math/floats` uses.

## Run

```sh
./make-subset.sh                 # builds build/ from ../sample/CoSy (POSIX sh + perl)
REVA=/path/to/reva build/run-cosy                # in the terminal
./cosy-desktop                                   # in a window, with CoSy's title and icon
./install-desktop.sh                             # Linux: add CoSy to the app launcher (once)
```

`cosy-desktop` runs `reva-desktop --package build` (building `build/` first
if needed; set `REVA_DESKTOP` if the app is not on `PATH`) and passes other
options on, e.g. `./cosy-desktop -e 'demo paste-tidy.txt'`. Windows:
`cosy-desktop.cmd`, after `sh make-subset.sh` in Git Bash (untested).

### The CoSy icon

The manifest brands the window (needs reva-fork's desktop branding, PR #19):
title `CoSy`, icon `cosy.png` (window and taskbar), and `id` `cosy`, which
becomes the Linux window class. `install-desktop.sh` adds
`~/.local/share/applications/cosy.desktop` (`StartupWMClass=cosy`) and the
icons, so GNOME, KDE and Xfce show CoSy's icon in the launcher and the dock
too. `--uninstall` removes them; rerun it if this checkout moves.

`icons/` holds the logo (`cosy-logo.jpg`) and what `icons/make-icons.sh`
makes from it, committed so builds need no ImageMagick: `cosy-16`…`cosy-512.png`,
`cosy.ico` (Windows shortcut) and `cosy.icns` (macOS). `cosy-banner.jpg` is
the wide logo at the top of the main README.

**macOS.** With reva-fork's desktop app from after 2026-10-25 (Dock icon at
run time), `./cosy-desktop` shows CoSy's icon in the Dock and the app
switcher once the window is up. For Finder, Launchpad, Spotlight and the
menu-bar name too, make a CoSy.app:

```sh
./make-cosy-app.sh            # or: just cosy-app   (CoSy.app in ~/Applications)
open ~/Applications/CoSy.app
```

The app is self-contained, so you can give it away
(`ditto -c -k --keepParent CoSy.app CoSy-mac.zip`): it holds a copy of
`reva-desktop`, `cosy.icns` and a fresh `build/` (in `Contents/Resources/cosy`).
The bundle is never written to; on first launch, and after a newer CoSy.app
replaces it, it copies the package to `~/Library/Application Support/CoSy`
(or `$COSY_HOME`) and runs it there, so CoSy's files live in that folder.
Upgrading (a rebuilt or newer CoSy.app) never replaces your dictionaries
(`.csy`, `.csd`, e.g. `CoSy.csy` after `save`) or files you added. Other
shipped files you edited are copied to `.cosy-backup/DATE/` before the new
version replaces them, and `.cosy-shipped/` keeps the files as last
installed, including the original dictionaries.
The bundle is ad-hoc signed; on another Mac, open it the first time with
right-click > Open (it is not notarized).

`./make-cosy-app.sh --dev` (`just cosy-app --dev`) makes a CoSy.app that runs
this checkout's `build/` instead, for working on CoSy. Rerun either after
rebuilding `reva-desktop`.

`build/` is a reva-fork desktop *package*: `make-subset.sh` writes its
`reva-package.json` (`start`: `start-cosy.f`). In the app, files CoSy writes
land in `build/`. See reva-fork's `docs/desktop.md` to build `reva-desktop`.

[DEMO.md](DEMO.md) is a step-by-step demo script (terminal, desktop app, Windows).

At `ok>`:

- `demo paste-tidy.txt` runs a script, printing each line and then its result.
- `pp cosy-fractals.f` lists a source file in colour: Forth words as in
  reva-fork, CoSy's verbs (from `cosy.tbl`) bold green. `slurp type` stays
  plain. Colour shows at a terminal and in the desktop app, browser and zip;
  piped, `pp` prints plain text. See reva-fork's `docs/highlight.md`.
- `see cdragon` shows a word's source (a `:` definition, or a `value`,
  `constant`, `variable`, `create` or `defer` line), also for files you
  `include`;
  `defs pets.f` lists the words a file defines (`defs` alone: every
  included file); `list pets.f` is `pp pets.f`; `files` lists this
  directory (`files *.csy` the dictionaries), with no shell, also in the
  browser; `help dup` describes a
  Reva word.
- `restart` starts a fresh CoSy.
- `bye` quits.

`restart` is reva-fork's built-in one: a fresh Reva that includes
`start-cosy.f` again, in the terminal and in the desktop app. A copy of
`run-cosy` named `restart` serves the OS shell after a hard crash, as
`restart.bat` did on Windows. (`run-cosy` still loops on exit status 3, for
older reva-fork builds; `reva start-cosy.f` from `build/` works the same.)

## Turtle fractals, the CoSy way

`cosy-fractals.f` draws fractals in reva-fork's graphics window (needs
reva-fork with turtle graphics, PR #20; see its `docs/turtle.md`):

```sh
./cosy-desktop -e 'include cosy-fractals.f' -e '12 cdragon'
```

then `5 ckoch`, `6 chilbert`, `7 csierpinski`, `12 cdragon` at `ok>`. Each
prints its segment count, then draws. On the CLI (`build/run-cosy`) there
is no window: `" dragon.svg" svg-save .` writes the drawing as SVG.

reva-fork's Forth versions (`needs turtle/fractals`) draw *while they
recurse*: one turtle call per segment. Here the curve is **data first**, built
with whole-list operations, and only then drawn in **one** call:

| Step | CoSy |
|---|---|
| L-system generation | `Lrules str c>i at ,/`: every character indexes its replacement, then raze |
| turns | `Lturn str c>i at`: one index into a 128-entry turn table |
| headings | `+\`: a running sum of the turns |
| steps that draw | `Ldraw str c>i at &`: where the mask is 1, then `at` |

switcher once the window is up. For Finder, Launchpad, Spotlight and the
menu-bar name too, make a CoSy.app:

```sh
./make-cosy-app.sh            # or: just cosy-app   (CoSy.app in ~/Applications)

```

right-click > Open (it is not notarized).

- `demo paste-tidy.txt` runs a script, printing each line and then its result.
- `pp cosy-fractals.f` lists a source file in colour: Forth words as in
  reva-fork, CoSy's verbs (from `cosy.tbl`) bold green. `slurp type` stays
  plain. Colour shows at a terminal and in the desktop app, browser and zip;
  piped, `pp` prints plain text. See reva-fork's `docs/highlight.md`.

  `include`;

reva-fork with turtle graphics, PR #20; see its `docs/turtle.md`):

./cosy-desktop -e 'include cosy-fractals.f' -e '12 cdragon'
```

prints its segment count, then draws. On the CLI (`build/run-cosy`) there
is no window: `" dragon.svg" svg-save .` writes the drawing as SVG.

recurse*: one turtle call per segment. Here the curve is **data first**, built
with whole-list operations, and only then drawn in **one** call:

|---|---|

| turns | `Lturn str c>i at`: one index into a 128-entry turn table |
| headings | `+\`: a running sum of the turns |
| steps that draw | `Ldraw str c>i at &`: where the mask is 1, then `at` |

(`unfold`). Between steps a curve is an ordinary list you can count (`rho`),
reverse, or combine before anything is drawn. No floats are needed:
headings are integer degrees, and the turtle does the trigonometry.

vx86 code and allocate, so building the list is slower than the Forth
recursion. Seven patches give the hottest primitives fast paths: `+i`, `-i` and
the other `eachDir` words, `+\`, `reverse`, `at` (a cell or char vector
indexed by an integer vector), `&`, `,/` (a list of strings) and `c>i`.
Other shapes run Bob's loops. On the native CLI (Linux, without → with
the fast paths): `16 cdragon` 2.3 → 0.5 s (Forth: about 0.15 s),
`7 chilbert` 5.6 → 1.1 s, `6 ckoch` 3.1 → 0.7 s, `8 csierpinski`
1.7 → 0.4 s. The REPL
stays responsive, and Stop works while it builds. Depths are capped at
Koch 6, Hilbert 7, Sierpinski 8 and dragon 16.

## The web demo zip

A zip you upload to any web host, unzip (a subfolder is fine), and open in a
browser: CoSy on reva-fork's WebAssembly VM, with the REPL on the left and
the turtle graphics on the right.

```sh
just cosy-zip                        # or: reva-fork-subset/make-cosy-zip.sh
#   → ../reva-fork/rust/target/web/cosy-web-VERSION.zip
```

It needs a reva-fork checkout beside this one (`../reva-fork`, on `dev`;
or set `REVA_FORK`) with Rust and rustup, plus `perl` and `zip`. The script
builds `build/` (make-subset.sh), then runs reva-fork's
`rust/scripts/make-web-zip.sh --package build --name cosy`, which builds
`reva.wasm` and writes the zip. Options pass through, e.g. `just cosy-zip
--version 2026.1028.0` or `--out ~/Desktop`.

Upload and try it:

```text
unzip cosy-web-VERSION.zip            # on the host, anywhere under the web root
#   open https://your.host/path/cosy-web-VERSION/
include cosy-fractals.f  12 cdragon   # at ok>
```

To try it locally the way a host serves it:
`python3 -m http.server -d ../reva-fork/rust/target/web 8000`, then open
http://localhost:8000/cosy-web-VERSION/.

Files you write in CoSy are kept in the browser's localStorage for that site
(scheme, host and port), under `reva:cosy:fs:`; the split position is kept
too. Moving the site to another host starts with no saved files. Details of
the page, the split view and the manifest: reva-fork `docs/web.md`.

In the browser, `save` keeps `R` in localStorage, and that copy then wins
over the `CoSy.csy` in `pkg/` at every load. Two words undo a save; both
take effect at the next `restart` (or reload):

- `restore`: the save before the last one (`CoSy.bk`) back, as Bob's
  `restore.bat` did.
- `original`: Bob's `CoSy.csy` as shipped (kept in the build as
  `CoSy.orig.csy`, which nothing writes); the current one goes to `CoSy.bk`
  first, so `restore` undoes it.

`check-web.sh` is the gate for the zip. It builds it, serves it from a
subfolder the way a host would, and drives it in headless Chromium with
empty localStorage: the boot log (`CoSy.csy` restored, `script0` run),
`Pi` from Bob's dictionary, floats, both demo scripts, `save` across a
reload and a `restart`, `original`, `restore`, a turtle fractal, and no
page errors. It needs `python3`, Node and Playwright (`npm i playwright`,
`npx playwright install chromium`):

```sh
REVA_FORK=../reva-fork reva-fork-subset/check-web.sh
```

**The zip contains Bob Armstrong's CoSy sources** (`pkg/`, patched by
`patch-cosy.pl`). Publish it only where Bob has agreed to share CoSy; do not
attach it to a GitHub release.

### cosy-serve: the same, as one binary

`cosy-serve` holds the web demo and a tiny web server in one file. Run it
and CoSy opens in your browser from http://127.0.0.1:8481/, with the REPL on
the left and the turtle graphics on the right. Ctrl-C stops it. Files you
write are kept by the browser for that address, so they are there on the
next run. A second launch just opens the browser on the running one.

```sh
just cosy-serve              # or: reva-fork-subset/make-cosy-serve.sh
#   macOS: universal binary (arm64 + x86_64); Linux: static musl binary
just cosy-serve linux windows   # on Linux: also a Windows .exe (needs mingw-w64)
#   → ../reva-fork/rust/target/serve/cosy-serve-VERSION-TARGET[.exe] (+ .sha256)
../reva-fork/rust/target/serve/cosy-serve-*-macos-universal     # run it
```

It is reva-fork's `reva-serve` (see reva-fork `docs/serve.md`) built with
`build/` as its package, port 8481 and the name `cosy`. Options: `--port N`,
`--no-open`, `--list` (the embedded files).

**The binary contains Bob Armstrong's CoSy sources**, like the zip. Build it
locally and share it only where Bob has agreed; do not attach it to a GitHub
release.

The **About** button (web page, zip, cosy-serve, desktop app) shows CoSy's
entry from the manifest's `about`: credits to Bob Armstrong and a link to
[CoSy.com](https://cosy.com/CoSy/), then the reva-fork version and build it
runs on. This repository is private, so the About dialog does not link it.

`make-subset.sh` writes the manifest the browser reads:
`build/reva-package.json` lists every `.f`, `.txt`, `.csy` and `.csd` file in `files` (a
static server cannot list a folder) and sets `"canvas": "split"`. The
desktop app reads the same manifest and opens CoSy in the split view too.

## Version

CoSy's version is in `../VERSION`: `YYYY.MMDD.N`. The first change to `dev` on
a day sets it to that day with `.0`, and it stays there for that day's other
changes until `dev` is merged into `main`; changes after that merge use `.1`,
`.2` and so on. It shows in the About dialog (manifest `about.version`), the
web zip's name (`cosy-web-VERSION.zip`), CoSy.app's Get Info and `csy`. The
cosy-serve binary's name still carries reva-fork's version (its
`build-serve.sh` has no `--version` yet).

## Files

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `make-subset.sh` | copies `../sample/CoSy/*.f` to `build/`, patches it, adds the files below |
| `patch-cosy.pl` | the 30 source patches; each must match the expected number of times or the build fails |
| `compat708.f` | Reva 7.0.8 words CoSy uses, on 2011.2: `>defer`, `make`, `undo`, a non-immediate `value` |
| `reva-gaps.f` | workarounds for reva-fork gaps, loaded before CoSy.f: `shell$` without `tempnam`, `(open-url)` for `www` |
| `tui-text.f` | `include tui-text.f`: the text side of Bob's Tui.f without windows; `res`, `text` and `state` are the R entries the windows were saved to (`>res`, `res>`, `->r`, `r>-`, `>text`, `text>`, `state>`, `type>res` ...) |
| `cosy-tools.f` | `see` (a word's source definition, from CoSy's, the package's, Reva's and included files; `xsee` is Reva's `see`), `defs`, `include` (notes the file for `see` and `defs`), `help` (from Reva's `help.txt`, copied into the package) and a `slurp` that reports a missing file name |
| `cosy-save.f` | `save`: `R` to `CoSyStartFile`, the last save to `CoSy.bk` (what the TUI's save did); `restore` (CoSy.bk back) and `original` (Bob's CoSy.csy back) |
| `start-cosy.f` | loader: compat708, CoSy.f, cosy-save.f, demo.f; the package's start file. Not named `cosy.f`, because case-insensitive file systems would treat that as `CoSy.f` |
| `demo.f` | `demo <file>`: echo each script line, then its result and the stack |
| `cosy-fractals.f` | turtle fractals as list operations (L-systems, `+\`, one bulk `path` call); `include` it on demand |
| `run-cosy` | POSIX sh launcher (cd to `build/`, run reva; REPL history in `~/.cosy_history`, or `$REVA_HISTORY`) |
| `cosy-desktop`, `cosy-desktop.cmd` | open CoSy in reva-desktop, in its own window with the CoSy icon |

#!/bin/sh
# make-web-zip.sh: build the browser REPL as a static site and zip it, ready
# to upload to any web host, unzip, and serve as plain files.
#
#   scripts/make-web-zip.sh [options]          (from anywhere; POSIX sh)
#
#   --package DIR   include DIR (a folder with reva-package.json) as pkg/ and
#                   open it by default; its manifest must list its "files"
#   --name NAME     zip and folder name (default: reva, or the package's id)
#   --version V     version in the name (default: the workspace version)
#   --canvas MODE   default graphics placement: split (default), pane, window
#   --out DIR       where the zip goes (default: target/web)
#   --no-build      use the reva.wasm already in components/web/crates/reva-web/www
#
# Result: OUT/NAME-web-V.zip holding one folder NAME-web-V/ (the site) and
# the same tree unzipped at OUT/NAME-web-V/ (what reva-serve embeds).
#
# The site is static and relative: index.html, the JS modules, reva.wasm,
# canvas.html and, with a package, pkg/.  It needs no server logic, no
# special headers (no SharedArrayBuffer, so no COOP/COEP), and works under
# any subpath (https://host/some/dir/NAME-web-V/).  Files written by Forth
# are kept in the visitor's localStorage, which is per origin: a site moved
# to another host or port starts with no saved files.
#
# The zip is reproducible: files are listed in sorted order and stamped
#!/bin/sh
# build-serve.sh: build reva-serve, the one-binary local web app, for
# release: the static site (make-web-zip.sh) embedded in a small server.
#
#   scripts/build-serve.sh [options] [TARGET ...]        (POSIX sh)
#
#   --site DIR      embed DIR (a site tree, e.g. from make-web-zip.sh)
#                   instead of building one
#   --package DIR   build the site with this package (make-web-zip.sh --package)
#   --name NAME     app name: binary NAME-serve (default: reva, or the package id)
#   --port N        preferred port (default 8421)
#   --out DIR       where binaries go (default: target/serve)
#   --no-build      do not rebuild reva.wasm
#
# TARGET is a Rust target triple, or one of these shorthands:
#   mac      universal macOS binary (arm64 + x86_64, joined with lipo; macOS only)
#   linux    static Linux binary for this machine's CPU (x86_64/aarch64 musl)
#   windows  x86_64-pc-windows-gnu (needs mingw-w64 when not on Windows)
# Default: mac on macOS, linux on Linux, the host triple elsewhere.
#

CoSy code must not be redistributed in any form from reva-fork: no sources,
no packages, no test fixtures or goldens that embed it, no web zips or
cosy-serve binaries in reva-fork's tree (even git-ignored target/), and
nothing CoSy on the published live demo.

test". Whether CoSy is published is up to Bob Armstrong; ba-cosy-zip-fork
is private.

pass `--out` to reva-fork scripts so output stays there (make-web-zip.sh
writes target/web by default), delete the CoSy builds when done, and in
docs describe commands and results without quoting CoSy source. Related:
[[shared-mac-no-focus-stealing]].

# Reva documentation

Documentation for the portable Reva core, rebuilt from the implementation in
[`components/`](../components/README.md). It replaces the old wiki in [`www/`](../www/), which
describes the deprecated x86 distribution (see [parity.md](parity.md) for
what has been carried over and what has not, yet).

| Page | Covers |
|---|---|
| [Getting started](getting-started.md) | building, the `reva` command, the browser build |
| [Gotchas](gotchas.md) | pitfalls, old and new |
| [Parity](parity.md) | old wiki topics and example programs vs. the portable core |
| [Example parity](parity-examples.md) | generated status of every program in `examples/` |
| [Demo script](demo.md) | step by step: what to type in the CLI, the browser and the desktop app, and what you see |
| [Packaging and Windows](packaging.md) | redistributable builds, license notices, installers, signing; building and testing on Windows 10+ |
| [REPL keys and history](repl.md) | Up/Down history, Ctrl-R search, Emacs line editing in every REPL |
| [Browser and static site](web.md) | URL options, the split view, `?package=`, the uploadable zip (`just web-zip`) |
| [reva-serve](serve.md) | the browser REPL (and a package) as one local binary per OS; release builds |
| [Desktop app](desktop.md) | `reva-desktop`: build, run, files on disk, packages |
| [Colour listings](highlight.md) | `pp FILE`, `hl-type`: syntax-highlighted Forth source in every REPL; the token table shared with the blog script |
| [Running Reva's x86](x86-plan.md) | how vx86 runs Reva's machine code and floats, `see`, what legacy programs can expect, what breaks and how it gets ported |
| [Plan: IUP programs](iup-plan.md) | high-level plan for running Reva's IUP GUI programs and CoSy's TUI, reimplemented in Rust with a Yew renderer |
| [The UI model](ui-model.md) | IUP's elements, attributes, callbacks, keys and layout (in character cells) as the Rust model the iup library and the TUI build on: scope and rules |
| [SQLite](sqlite.md) | `needs db/sqlite`: databases through the `~db` words; built into the CLI, desktop and browser next |
| [Turtle graphics](turtle.md) | `~turtle`: Logo-style drawing in a graphics window; fractal demos; SVG |
| [Portability](portability.md) | what stops on the portable core (native libraries, `shell`, x87/SIMD) and why |
| [Licenses](licenses.md) | third-party files, their licenses, and the no-copyleft check |
| [Design](design.md) | how the portable core works and why |
| [sed-rs asks](sed-rs-asks.md) | what this repository needs from an updated sed-rs (in-place editing, ranges, literal patterns), from using it here |
| [Code metrics](code-metrics.md) | how the Rust code is shaped: components, limits, rules, and what to do when a part is full |

## Conventions: every sample is executed

A Forth sample is a `forth` block followed by an `output` block:

```forth
: sq dup * ;
7 sq .
```
```output
49
```

`scripts/doc-check.sh` feeds each `forth` block to a fresh `reva` and
compares the result with the `output` block (ignoring trailing spaces); the
regression suite runs it over these pages. A page cannot drift from the
implementation without a test failing. When adding a sample, run it first and
paste what `reva` actually prints, then check that it is *right*.

input.content:
# CoSy in reva-fork

[CoSy](https://cosy.com/CoSy/) is Bob Armstrong's APL-inspired language
built on Reva Forth, and reva-fork's main user. This page lists the ways to
run it on reva-fork, and which of them work today and which are planned.

**This repository holds no CoSy code, and never will.** Not its sources, not
a package, not test fixtures or goldens, not the live demo. Whether and
where CoSy is published is up to Bob. The CoSy package is built in the
private repository
[ba-cosy-zip-fork](https://github.com/softwarewrighter/ba-cosy-zip-fork)
(the "CoSy lane"), which patches Bob's sources and adds launchers. Its
`reva-fork-subset/README.md` and `DEMO.md` are the detailed instructions.
Everything below runs a package you build there, on your own machine.

Status checked on 2026-11-01 against reva-fork `dev` (2026.1101.0, after
steps 33 to 35), from a scratch copy of ba-cosy-zip-fork's `dev`.

## The package

```text
cd ba-cosy-zip-fork
reva-fork-subset/make-subset.sh      # → reva-fork-subset/build/, a reva-fork package
```

`build/` is a [package](web.md): a folder with `reva-package.json`
(`start`: `start-cosy.f`). Every host below runs it. When CoSy starts it
loads its sources, restores `CoSy.csy` into its dictionary `R` and runs the
script stored there.

## At a glance

| Way | Status | How |
|---|---|---|
| CLI REPL | **works** | `cd build && reva start-cosy.f` (or `build/run-cosy`) |
| CLI, piped or scripted | **works** | `reva start-cosy.f -e '...'`, or input on stdin |
| CLI drawings as files | **works** | `reva --draw png start-cosy.f`, then `include cosy-fractals.f` and `12 cdragon` |
| reva-fork's notebook, in the terminal | **works** | `needs ui/notebook notebook` at CoSy's `ok>` |
| Browser, local (`cosy-serve`) | **works** | `scripts/build-serve.sh --package build --name cosy` (see [below](#browser-and-desktop)) |
| reva-fork's notebook, in the browser | **works** | `needs ui/notebook notebook` at CoSy's `ok>` |
| Browser, on a web host (zip) | works, not published | `scripts/make-web-zip.sh --package build --name cosy`; publish only where Bob agrees |
| Desktop app | works (ba-cosy) | `cosy-desktop` or `CoSy.app` from ba-cosy-zip-fork; not re-run on 2026-11-01 |
| ba-cosy's `just cosy-zip`, `just cosy-serve` | **broken** | they call reva-fork's old paths; workaround below |
| Bob's `Tui.f` windows (IUP) | planned | step 40 `local-tui-cosy` |
| Upload a file or package into the page | planned | step 37 `local-web-upload` |
| One saved image (`--image`) | **not yet** | step 38 `local-image-everywhere` |
| A published site (e.g. cosy.softwarewrighter.com) | planned, Bob's call | step 39 `local-publish-package` |

## The CLI

```text
cd ba-cosy-zip-fork/reva-fork-subset/build
reva start-cosy.f                    # the REPL; `bye` quits, `restart` starts over
reva start-cosy.f -e 'demo paste-tidy.txt' -e bye     # a scripted run
```

# Reva documentation

Documentation for the portable Reva core, rebuilt from the implementation in
[`components/`](../components/README.md). It replaces the old wiki in [`www/`](../www/), which
describes the deprecated x86 distribution (see [parity.md](parity.md) for
what has been carried over and what has not, yet).

| Page | Covers |
|---|---|
| [Getting started](getting-started.md) | building, the `reva` command, the browser build |
| [Gotchas](gotchas.md) | pitfalls, old and new |
| [Parity](parity.md) | old wiki topics and example programs vs. the portable core |
| [Example parity](parity-examples.md) | generated status of every program in `examples/` |
| [Demo script](demo.md) | step by step: what to type in the CLI, the browser and the desktop app, and what you see |
| [Packaging and Windows](packaging.md) | redistributable builds, license notices, installers, signing; building and testing on Windows 10+ |
| [REPL keys and history](repl.md) | Up/Down history, Ctrl-R search, Emacs line editing in every REPL |
| [Browser and static site](web.md) | URL options, the split view, `?package=`, the uploadable zip (`just web-zip`) |
| [reva-serve](serve.md) | the browser REPL (and a package) as one local binary per OS; release builds |
| [Desktop app](desktop.md) | `reva-desktop`: build, run, files on disk, packages |
| [Colour listings](highlight.md) | `pp FILE`, `hl-type`: syntax-highlighted Forth source in every REPL; the token table shared with the blog script |
| [Running Reva's x86](x86-plan.md) | how vx86 runs Reva's machine code and floats, `see`, what legacy programs can expect, what breaks and how it gets ported |
| [Plan: IUP programs](iup-plan.md) | high-level plan for running Reva's IUP GUI programs and CoSy's TUI, reimplemented in Rust with a Yew renderer |
| [The UI model](ui-model.md) | IUP's elements, attributes, callbacks, keys and layout (in character cells) as the Rust model the iup library and the TUI build on: scope and rules |
| [SQLite](sqlite.md) | `needs db/sqlite`: databases through the `~db` words; built into the CLI, desktop and browser next |
| [Turtle graphics](turtle.md) | `~turtle`: Logo-style drawing in a graphics window; fractal demos; SVG |
| [Portability](portability.md) | what stops on the portable core (native libraries, `shell`, x87/SIMD) and why |
| [Licenses](licenses.md) | third-party files, their licenses, and the no-copyleft check |
| [Design](design.md) | how the portable core works and why |
| [sed-rs asks](sed-rs-asks.md) | what this repository needs from an updated sed-rs (in-place editing, ranges, literal patterns), from using it here |
| [Code metrics](code-metrics.md) | how the Rust code is shaped: components, limits, rules, and what to do when a part is full |

## Conventions: every sample is executed

A Forth sample is a `forth` block followed by an `output` block:

```forth
: sq dup * ;
7 sq .
```
```output
49
```

`scripts/doc-check.sh` feeds each `forth` block to a fresh `reva` and
compares the result with the `output` block (ignoring trailing spaces); the
regression suite runs it over these pages. A page cannot drift from the
implementation without a test failing. When adding a sample, run it first and
paste what `reva` actually prints, then check that it is *right*.

where CoSy is published is up to Bob. The CoSy package is built in the
private repository
[ba-cosy-zip-fork](https://github.com/softwarewrighter/ba-cosy-zip-fork)
(the "CoSy lane"), which patches Bob's sources and adds launchers. Its
`reva-fork-subset/README.md` and `DEMO.md` are the detailed instructions.
Everything below runs a package you build there, on your own machine.

Status checked on 2026-11-01 against reva-fork `dev` (2026.1101.0, after
steps 33 to 35), from a scratch copy of ba-cosy-zip-fork's `dev`.

## The package

```text
cd ba-cosy-zip-fork
reva-fork-subset/make-subset.sh      # → reva-fork-subset/build/, a reva-fork package
```

`build/` is a [package](web.md): a folder with `reva-package.json`
(`start`: `start-cosy.f`). Every host below runs it. When CoSy starts it
loads its sources, restores `CoSy.csy` into its dictionary `R` and runs the
script stored there.

## At a glance

| Way | Status | How |
|---|---|---|
| CLI REPL | **works** | `cd build && reva start-cosy.f` (or `build/run-cosy`) |
| CLI, piped or scripted | **works** | `reva start-cosy.f -e '...'`, or input on stdin |
| CLI drawings as files | **works** | `reva --draw png start-cosy.f`, then `include cosy-fractals.f` and `12 cdragon` |
| reva-fork's notebook, in the terminal | **works** | `needs ui/notebook notebook` at CoSy's `ok>` |
| Browser, local (`cosy-serve`) | **works** | `scripts/build-serve.sh --package build --name cosy` (see [below](#browser-and-desktop)) |
| reva-fork's notebook, in the browser | **works** | `needs ui/notebook notebook` at CoSy's `ok>` |
| Browser, on a web host (zip) | works, not published | `scripts/make-web-zip.sh --package build --name cosy`; publish only where Bob agrees |
| Desktop app | works (ba-cosy) | `cosy-desktop` or `CoSy.app` from ba-cosy-zip-fork; not re-run on 2026-11-01 |
| ba-cosy's `just cosy-zip`, `just cosy-serve` | **broken** | they call reva-fork's old paths; workaround below |
| Bob's `Tui.f` windows (IUP) | planned | step 40 `local-tui-cosy` |
| Upload a file or package into the page | planned | step 37 `local-web-upload` |
| One saved image (`--image`) | **not yet** | step 38 `local-image-everywhere` |
| A published site (e.g. cosy.softwarewrighter.com) | planned, Bob's call | step 39 `local-publish-package` |

## The CLI

```text
cd ba-cosy-zip-fork/reva-fork-subset/build
reva start-cosy.f                    # the REPL; `bye` quits, `restart` starts over
reva start-cosy.f -e 'demo paste-tidy.txt' -e bye     # a scripted run
```

Checked: CoSy boots in about half a second, and its demo script
(`demo paste-tidy.txt`: vectors, reduce, reshape, strings, the dictionary)
prints the expected result for every line.

**Drawings.** The CLI has no graphics window, so each turtle drawing goes to
a new file ([turtle.md](turtle.md#the-cli-drawings-as-files)). With
`--draw png`, CoSy's `include cosy-fractals.f` and `12 cdragon` write
`turtle-001.png` (4,096 segments), never over an existing file. In iTerm2
or WezTerm the default `--draw auto` also shows the PNG inline.

**The notebook.** `needs ui/notebook notebook` opens reva-fork's TUI
notebook full screen in the terminal, over CoSy: a CoSy line evaluated with
Ctrl-J shows its result in the lower pane. Checked in tmux. The notebook
keeps its text in `notebook.txt` in the package folder.

## Browser and desktop

The browser page, `reva-serve` and the desktop app run the same web page,
with CoSy's REPL on the left and the turtle graphics on the right
(`"canvas": "split"` in the manifest).

**cosy-serve: one local binary.** reva-fork's
[reva-serve](serve.md) built with the package:

```text
reva-fork/scripts/build-serve.sh --package ba-cosy-zip-fork/reva-fork-subset/build \
    --name cosy --port 8481 --out /some/private/folder
/some/private/folder/cosy-serve-VERSION-macos-universal     # opens http://127.0.0.1:8481/
```

Checked: CoSy boots in the page; `?eval=include%20cosy-fractals.f&eval=12%20cdragon`
draws the dragon beside the REPL; `needs ui/notebook notebook` opens the
notebook, and a CoSy line evaluated there shows its result. Pass `--out`:
by default the scripts write into reva-fork's `target/`, and CoSy builds
should not sit in this checkout.

**A web host: the zip.** `scripts/make-web-zip.sh --package ... --name cosy
--out ...` makes a static site to unzip anywhere under a web root
([web.md](web.md)). Files CoSy writes stay in the visitor's browser
storage. The binary and the zip both contain Bob's sources: share them only
where he agrees.

**The desktop app.** ba-cosy-zip-fork's `cosy-desktop` runs
`reva-desktop --package build` in a window with CoSy's title and icon;
`make-cosy-app.sh` makes a self-contained macOS `CoSy.app`. Both are the
CoSy lane's and were not re-run here; the desktop app shows the same page
as the browser, which was.

**Broken today: ba-cosy's wrappers.** `just cosy-zip` and `just cosy-serve`
in ba-cosy-zip-fork call `$REVA_FORK/rust/scripts/make-web-zip.sh` and
`rust/scripts/build-serve.sh`, and expect output in `rust/target/`. Since
reva-fork's components restructuring these are `scripts/` and `target/` at
the root, with the same options. Until the CoSy lane updates its paths, run
reva-fork's scripts directly as above.

## Planned

- **Bob's windows, `Tui.f` and `Job.f`** (step 40 `local-tui-cosy`): the
  IUP dialogs CoSy's TUI is made of, through reva-fork's virtual IUP
  library ([iup-plan.md](iup-plan.md), [ui-model.md](ui-model.md)), in the
  terminal, the browser and the desktop app. ba-cosy's `tui-text.f` covers
  the text side today.
- **Upload into the page** (step 37 `local-web-upload`): an Upload button
  for a Forth file or a whole package, kept in browser storage (IndexedDB or
  OPFS for large files), with storage pluggable so that, for example, a
  CoSy host can keep notebooks on its own server.
- **One file to ship** (step 38 `local-image-everywhere`): a saved image
  that starts in the CLI, the page and the desktop app. Not yet for CoSy:
  `--save-image` after loading CoSy writes an image, but `--image` with it
  shows CoSy's depth display and then neither results nor a prompt.
- **A published site** (step 39 `local-publish-package`): a package or
  image behind its own domain, such as cosy.softwarewrighter.com, only if
  Bob wants CoSy published that way. Otherwise reva-fork is hosted alone,
  and CoSy is hosted by Bob.

What CoSy needs from reva-fork, by priority, is tracked in
ba-cosy-zip-fork's `docs/reva-fork-asks.md`.

#!/bin/sh
# make-web-zip.sh: build the browser REPL as a static site and zip it, ready
# to upload to any web host, unzip, and serve as plain files.
#
#   scripts/make-web-zip.sh [options]          (from anywhere; POSIX sh)
#
#   --package DIR   include DIR (a folder with reva-package.json) as pkg/ and
#                   open it by default; its manifest must list its "files"
#   --name NAME     zip and folder name (default: reva, or the package's id)
#   --version V     version in the name (default: the workspace version)
#   --canvas MODE   default graphics placement: split (default), pane, window
#   --out DIR       where the zip goes (default: target/web)
#   --no-build      use the reva.wasm already in components/web/crates/reva-web/www
#
# Result: OUT/NAME-web-V.zip holding one folder NAME-web-V/ (the site) and
# the same tree unzipped at OUT/NAME-web-V/ (what reva-serve embeds).
#
# The site is static and relative: index.html, the JS modules, reva.wasm,
# canvas.html and, with a package, pkg/.  It needs no server logic, no
# special headers (no SharedArrayBuffer, so no COOP/COEP), and works under
# any subpath (https://host/some/dir/NAME-web-V/).  Files written by Forth
# are kept in the visitor's localStorage, which is per origin: a site moved
# to another host or port starts with no saved files.
#
# The zip is reproducible: files are listed in sorted order and stamped
# with the last commit's time (UTC), so the same commit gives the same zip.
set -eu
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd "$HERE/.." && pwd)
WWW=$ROOT/components/web/crates/reva-web/www
PKG= NAME= VERSION= CANVAS=split OUT=$ROOT/target/web BUILD=1

die() { echo "make-web-zip: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case $1 in
        --package) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "$1 needs a value"; PKG=$2; shift 2 ;;
        --name) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "$1 needs a value"; NAME=$2; shift 2 ;;
        --version) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "$1 needs a value"; VERSION=$2; shift 2 ;;
        --canvas) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "$1 needs a value"; CANVAS=$2; shift 2 ;;
        --out) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "$1 needs a value"; OUT=$2; shift 2 ;;
        --no-build) BUILD=; shift ;;
        -h|--help) sed -n '2,25p' "$0" | cut -c3-; exit 0 ;;
        *) die "unknown option $1 (try --help)" ;;
    esac
done

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The gate: everything that must pass before a commit (`just check`).
#
#   scripts/check.sh            all of it
#   scripts/check.sh --fast     skip the desktop component (Tauri)
#
# Runs, and stops at the first failure:
#   1. every component (components/*, one Cargo workspace each) but the
#      desktop: cargo fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, tests (release);
#      and every component on the same version
#   2. the WebAssembly build and its node tests
#   3. components/desktop: cargo fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, tests
#   4. the reg-rs goldens on the release CLI; a failure is accepted only
#      if KNOWN_FAILURES lists it for this OS
#   5. the license check
#   6. sw-checklist: its FAIL count may not exceed SW_CHECKLIST_MAX_FAILS
#
# Bash 3.2 compatible (macOS /bin/bash).
set -euo pipefail
root="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"

# Goldens known to fail, per OS, until the step that fixes them
# (.agentrail: local-portable-gates).  The list may only shrink.
case "$(uname)" in
    Darwin) KNOWN_FAILURES="docs-samples" ;;
    *)      KNOWN_FAILURES="" ;;
esac

# sw-checklist FAILs: 51 on 2026-10-26, 49 after edition 2024, 47 after
# the web checks, 46 after the split of reva-vm, 40 after the word
# families (local-comp-words), 27 after vx86 (local-comp-x86), 22 after the
# machine (local-comp-core), 18 after the host (local-comp-host), 15 after
# vlib (local-comp-vlib), 7 after the CLI (local-comp-cli), 0 after the
# front ends (local-comp-front-ends).  It stays 0: the checklist is required.
SW_CHECKLIST_MAX_FAILS=0

fast=0
[[ "${1:-}" == --fast ]] && fast=1

step() { printf '\n== %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\ncheck: FAILED: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }

# The components the core builds from, dependencies first; the desktop
# (Tauri, a few hundred crates) is step 3.
COMPONENTS="macros x86-types x86-decode x86-alu x86-exec x86 host-base vfs host core-parts canvas ui ui-layout ui-grid ui-web core core-run iup vlib words-base words-interp words-dict words-os words vm sqlite cli-edit cli-host cli web serve"

version() { awk -F'"' '/^version *=/ { print $2; exit }' "$root/components/$1/Cargo.toml"; }
for c in $COMPONENTS; do
    step "components/$c: fmt, clippy, tests"
    (cd "$root/components/$c" && cargo fmt --check) || fail "$c: cargo fmt --check (run cargo fmt in components/$c)"
    (cd "$root/components/$c" && cargo clippy -q --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings) || fail "$c: clippy"
    (cd "$root/components/$c" && cargo test -q --release --workspace) || fail "$c: tests"
    [[ "$(version "$c")" == "$(version vm)" ]] || fail "$c: version $(version "$c"), not $(version vm) as components/vm"
done

step "web: wasm build, node tests"
"$root/scripts/build-web.sh" >/dev/null || fail "web: build-web.sh"
for t in smoke lineedit ansi; do
    node "$root/components/web/crates/reva-web/test/$t.mjs" >/dev/null || fail "web: test/$t.mjs (run it for details)"
done

if [[ $fast -eq 0 ]]; then
    step "desktop: fmt, clippy, tests"
    (cd "$root/components/desktop" && cargo fmt --check) || fail "desktop: cargo fmt --check"
    "$root/components/desktop/build.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "desktop: build.sh (run it for details)"
    (cd "$root/components/desktop" && cargo clippy -q --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings) || fail "desktop: clippy"
    (cd "$root/components/desktop" && cargo test -q --workspace) || fail "desktop: tests"
fi

step "goldens (reg-rs, release CLI)"
out=$(cd "$root" && REVA=target/release/reva scripts/regress.sh 2>&1) || true
echo "$out" | grep -E 'passed|FAIL' || fail "goldens: no summary from regress.sh"
unexpected=""
for t in $(echo "$out" | sed -n 's/^ *FAIL: *//p'); do
    case " $KNOWN_FAILURES " in
        *" $t "*) echo "   (known failure on $(uname): $t)" ;;
        *)        unexpected="$unexpected $t" ;;
    esac
done
[[ -z "$unexpected" ]] || fail "goldens:$unexpected (details: REVA=target/release/reva scripts/regress.sh -v -p NAME)"

step "licenses"
"$root/scripts/license-check.sh" || fail "license-check.sh"

step "sw-checklist"
# sw-checklist exits 1 while it has FAILs; the count below is the test.
summary=$(cd "$root" && { sw-checklist 2>&1 || true; } | grep '^Summary:') || fail "sw-checklist did not run"
echo "$summary"
fails=$(echo "$summary" | sed -n 's/.* \([0-9][0-9]*\) failed.*/\1/p')
[[ -n "$fails" ]] || fail "sw-checklist: cannot read the FAIL count"
[[ "$fails" -le "$SW_CHECKLIST_MAX_FAILS" ]] ||
    fail "sw-checklist: $fails FAILs, more than $SW_CHECKLIST_MAX_FAILS (sw-checklist -v | grep FAIL)"

printf '\ncheck: ok\n'

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

tools.name: Monitor
tools.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.
