# Gotchas

Rebuilt from the old wiki's `gotchas.wiki`; every sample runs on the
portable core. Items that depend on parts not yet ported are listed at the
end.

## `'` vs `[']`

Both give the *xt* (execution token) of a word, but `'` parses the next
word *when it runs*. Inside a definition that means: when the definition is
executed, not when it is compiled. Use `[']` inside definitions to get the xt
of the word that follows in the source.

```forth
: sq dup * ;
: sq-xt ['] sq ;
4 sq-xt catch . .
```
```output
0 16
```

(`catch` runs an xt and leaves 0 when nothing was thrown.) With `'`, the word
is taken from the input when `later` runs:

```forth
: sq dup * ;
: later ' ;
later sq 5 swap catch . .
```
```output
0 25
```

## Character constants

`'A` is not a word: it is the number 65, the character code of `A`. So
`'(` and `'"` are character constants, not functions.

```forth
'A . '( emit '" emit cr
```
```output
65 ("
```

## Singles and doubles are integers

A trailing `L` makes a double-cell integer; it is pushed low cell first, so
the high cell is on top. Neither is a narrower kind of float.

```forth
1234L . .
-1L . .
```
```output
0 1234 -1 -1
```

## Number range

Numbers are 32-bit cells. Literals are checked for overflow, so
`-2147483648` (the most negative cell) cannot be typed directly; compute it.

```forth
2147483647 .
-2147483647 1- .
2147483647 1+ .
```
```output
2147483647 -2147483648 -2147483648
```

## An error in an included file stops that file

Typed at the prompt, an unknown word only skips the rest of its line. In a
file read with `include` (or given on the command line), the first unknown
word abandons the *rest of the file*, and the stack is restored to what it
was before the `include`. Check the first `ERROR:` line in the output: it
starts with the file and line, and the files that included it, as a
compiler's do (`inner.f:3 (from outer.f:7): ERROR: unknown word: ...`).
A fault says where too, and shows the stack:

```text
*** bad memory access: 4 byte(s) at 0x00000000 (in bad+0xc, eip ...) at outer.f:7 after `bad`
stack (4): 2 7 8 0
```

A file that is not there is reported (`include: nosuch.f: no such file`)
and `ioerr` is 1; the original Reva said nothing.

## Stack underflow is a warning

A word that takes more than the stack holds (`drop` on an empty stack)
prints ``warning: stack underflow (depth -1) at FILE:LINE after `drop` `` once, and Forth goes on, as
Reva did: words run in the slack above the stack, and later pushes bring it
back. Programs written for Reva rely on it (CoSy's Tui.f, and
`examples/sqlite.f`). `reva --underflow fail` stops with an error instead.

## Times are UTC

`time&date` and `localtime` report UTC: the portable core has no time-zone
database. The clock comes from the host (in the browser, the page passes
`Date.now()` in before each slice).

## Files: `ioerr` is `-errno`, and the browser keeps files in memory

The file words keep the original's results: after `open/r`, `read`,
`write`, `close`, `delete`, `rename`, `chdir`, ... `ioerr` is 0 on
success and the negative Linux `errno` on failure (`-2` for a missing
file), and a failed `open/r` returns that same negative number as the
"handle". Test `ioerr @`, not the handle.

Quirks of `reva.f` itself (unchanged, as on Linux x86):

- `rename ( a1 n1 a2 n2 -- )` removes one more cell than it takes (its
  system call reads three arguments). Keep a spare cell under the names.
- `seek ( offs h -- )` leaves nothing; use `tell` for the position.
- `creat` opens for writing only; reopen with `open/r` or `open/rw` to read.

`lib/` is built into the core and appears at `/reva/lib/` (read-only)
even without the files on disk, so `needs` works everywhere. In the
browser all files are in memory: the page bundles its own, and what Forth
code writes, or you upload, is kept in IndexedDB (the browser's quota for
the site; older pages used localStorage's 5 MB, moved over at first start). Empty directories are not kept, and modification times there
read as 0.

## Stop in the browser

**Stop** (Ctrl-C) takes effect within one slice, about 8 ms, and acts like
a fault: the rest of the input is dropped and a half-made definition is
removed. Code running inside a host callback (a redefined `emit`, `type` or
`cr`) cannot be interrupted that way; after 2 seconds the page replaces the
worker with a fresh one. Saved files survive that, but the session's
definitions are lost.

## A runaway loop pauses

A word that never ends, like `: spin repeat again ; spin` (or a word whose
last call is itself, which Reva compiles as a jump), would keep a CPU core
busy. In the browser and the desktop app, after 5 seconds of running
without waiting for input, the VM pauses: it uses no CPU, and a bar offers
**Stop**, **5 s more** or **Keep going**. A hidden tab pauses it as well,
and it goes on when the tab is shown again (`?background` in the URL keeps
it running). The CLI stops a run with `*** time limit` and exit status 124
after `reva --max-cpu SECONDS`. That limit defaults to 30 seconds with
`--ui-script` and is off otherwise (Ctrl-C stops a run at a terminal).

## `save` writes an image, not an executable

`save NAME` (and `(save)`, which takes `a n`) writes a vx86 image, about
1.5 MB, that starts with `reva --image NAME` or in the browser; it is not a
program you can run by itself, and `makeexename` adds no extension.
`makeexe` is not available. An image starts as the saved executable did:
`onstartup` handlers, then the banner and prompt, with no file being
included. A prompt turned off when saving (piped input) stays off.

`restart` runs the `onexit` handlers, as `bye` does, then starts again
from the same boot or image. The rest of the line it is on is not run.
A file that always calls `restart` restarts for ever (Ctrl-C stops it).

## Floats are doubles inside

The original kept floats in the x87's 80-bit registers; the portable core
keeps them as 64-bit doubles. Loading an 80-bit value (`f@`, CoSy's
stored floats) rounds it to the nearest double, and results can differ
from the original in the last digits of extended precision. Because `f.`
cuts digits instead of rounding, that can show: `30 s>f deg>rad fsin f.`
prints `0.49999`. The rounding mode set with `round.even`, `round.trunc`
etc. applies to conversion to integers (`f>s`, `fround`, `fint`), not to
arithmetic.

## C functions: only a virtual libc

`lib`/`func:` work as before, but the only library is a virtual libc with
`getenv`, `putenv`, `localtime`, `opendir`/`readdir`/`closedir` and
`errno`. Any other library or function
fails to load, and `reva.f` reports it when the function is first called:
`ERROR: could not load <name>`. Native libraries are roadmap item 4.

## Pending (not yet ported)

- *Using a `func` as an xt* (from the old page): applies once foreign
  function calls (`func:`) are ported; the advice stands — wrap the `func`
  in a colon definition before passing its xt to `onexit` or `catch`.

content.text:
Ask 18 is solved, and the fix needed is a one-line change in the CoSy lane's own loader, not in reva-fork.

**What's happening:** Bob's Tui.f `>text` passes the string to `onvan`, whose `swap ref0del` frees one item from *below* the string. With an empty stack, that item is a leftover: whatever value the top-of-stack register (EAX) last held.
- **After a full source load,** the leftover happens to be a live CoSy object, so freeing it does nothing.
- **reva.f's `reset` sets the leftover to 0.** It runs when any saved program starts, so every image start, and after every error at the prompt. Bob's Reva 7.0 has the identical `reset`.
- **So it isn't specific to images:** from source, typing anything that errors and then `go` faults the same way. On Bob's Windows Reva it would crash too.
- **reva-fork matches Reva exactly here.** That's the proof the "Bob's files are never the bug" rule asks for, so I made no code change.

**Fix for the CoSy lane:** in `cosy-resume.f` (or wherever their shim calls `go`), give the leftover a harmless value first:
```forth
nil swap drop
```
I checked it in a scratch build, since deleted. With that line, `go` opens Bob's window both from the image and after an error in source mode. The CoSy lane can then go back to starting from the image by default, dropping its `COSY_IMAGE=1` opt-in.

PR #82 is docs only: a new section in `docs/gotchas.md` called "What lies under an empty stack". Next in the saga is step 48 `local-web-fresh-files`, CoSy's ask 16 about stale browser files after a rebuild.

#!/bin/sh
# make-web-zip.sh: build the browser REPL as a static site and zip it, ready
# to upload to any web host, unzip, and serve as plain files.
#
#   scripts/make-web-zip.sh [options]          (from anywhere; POSIX sh)
#
#   --package DIR   include DIR (a folder with reva-package.json) as pkg/ and
#                   open it by default; its manifest must list its "files"
#   --name NAME     zip and folder name (default: reva, or the package's id)
#   --version V     version in the name (default: the workspace version)
#   --canvas MODE   default graphics placement: split (default), pane, window
#   --out DIR       where the zip goes (default: target/web)
#   --no-build      use the reva.wasm already in components/web/crates/reva-web/www
#
# Result: OUT/NAME-web-V.zip holding one folder NAME-web-V/ (the site) and
# the same tree unzipped at OUT/NAME-web-V/ (what reva-serve embeds).
#
# The site is static and relative: index.html, the JS modules, reva.wasm,
# canvas.html and, with a package, pkg/.  It needs no server logic, no
# special headers (no SharedArrayBuffer, so no COOP/COEP), and works under
# any subpath (https://host/some/dir/NAME-web-V/).  Files written by Forth
# are kept in the visitor's localStorage, which is per origin: a site moved
# to another host or port starts with no saved files.
#
# The zip is reproducible: files are listed in sorted order and stamped
# with the last commit's time (UTC), so the same commit gives the same zip.
set -eu
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd "$HERE/.." && pwd)
WWW=$ROOT/components/web/crates/reva-web/www
PKG= NAME= VERSION= CANVAS=split OUT=$ROOT/target/web BUILD=1

die() { echo "make-web-zip: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case $1 in
        --package) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "$1 needs a value"; PKG=$2; shift 2 ;;
        --name) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "$1 needs a value"; NAME=$2; shift 2 ;;
        --version) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "$1 needs a value"; VERSION=$2; shift 2 ;;
        --canvas) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "$1 needs a value"; CANVAS=$2; shift 2 ;;
        --out) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "$1 needs a value"; OUT=$2; shift 2 ;;
        --no-build) BUILD=; shift ;;
        -h|--help) sed -n '2,25p' "$0" | cut -c3-; exit 0 ;;
        *) die "unknown option $1 (try --help)" ;;
    esac
done
case $CANVAS in split|pane|window) ;; *) die "--canvas $CANVAS: use split, pane or window" ;; esac
command -v zip >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "needs zip (macOS has it; Debian/Ubuntu: apt install zip)"

if [ -n "$PKG" ]; then
    [ -f "$PKG/reva-package.json" ] || die "$PKG: no reva-package.json"
    PKG=$(cd "$PKG" && pwd)
    grep -q '"files"' "$PKG/reva-package.json" \
        || die "$PKG/reva-package.json has no \"files\" list (a static server cannot list a folder)"
    if [ -z "$NAME" ]; then
        # the manifest's "id", else the folder name
        NAME=$(tr -d '\n' < "$PKG/reva-package.json" | awk '{ if (match($0, /"id"[ \t]*:[ \t]*"[A-Za-z0-9._-]+"/)) { s = substr($0, RSTART, RLENGTH); sub(/.*"id"[ \t]*:[ \t]*"/, "", s); sub(/"$/, "", s); print s } }')
        [ -n "$NAME" ] || NAME=$(basename "$PKG")
    fi
fi
NAME=${NAME:-reva}
case $NAME in *[!A-Za-z0-9._-]*|'') die "--name $NAME: use letters, digits, . _ -" ;; esac
if [ -z "$VERSION" ]; then
    VERSION=$(awk -F'"' '/^version *=/ { print $2; exit }' "$ROOT/components/vm/Cargo.toml")
fi

[ -n "$BUILD" ] && "$HERE/build-web.sh" >/dev/null
[ -f "$WWW/reva.wasm" ] || die "no $WWW/reva.wasm (run without --no-build)"

SITE=$NAME-web-$VERSION
mkdir -p "$OUT"
OUT=$(cd "$OUT" && pwd)
STAGE=$OUT/$SITE
ZIP=$OUT/$SITE.zip
rm -rf "$STAGE" "$ZIP"
mkdir -p "$STAGE"
for f in index.html host.js reva.js reva-worker.js reva.wasm ui.js tui.js canvas.html split.js package.js about.js lineedit.js ansi.js sqlite.js store.js upload.js favicon.png favicon.ico; do
    cp "$WWW/$f" "$STAGE/$f"
done
cp -R "$WWW/ui" "$STAGE/ui"
cp "$ROOT/LICENSE" "$STAGE/LICENSE.txt"
cp "$ROOT/LICENSE-MIT" "$STAGE/LICENSE-MIT.txt"

# The page's defaults and the build stamp (About), as meta tags (index.html reads them when the URL
# has no ?package= or ?canvas=).
pkgmeta=
if [ -n "$PKG" ]; then
    mkdir -p "$STAGE/pkg"
    # every file of the package except dot files (.git and friends)
    (cd "$PKG" && find . -type f ! -path '*/.*' | while IFS= read -r f; do
        mkdir -p "$STAGE/pkg/$(dirname "$f")"
        cp "$f" "$STAGE/pkg/$f"
    done)
    pkgmeta=pkg/
fi
build=$("$HERE/build-stamp.sh")
awk -v pkg="$pkgmeta" -v canvas="$CANVAS" -v build="$build" '
    index($0, "<meta name=\"reva-package\" content=\"\">") { sub(/content=""/, "content=\"" pkg "\"") }
    index($0, "<meta name=\"reva-canvas\" content=\"\">") { sub(/content=""/, "content=\"" canvas "\"") }
    index($0, "<meta name=\"reva-build\" content=\"\">") { sub(/content=""/, "content=\"" build "\"") }
    { print }' "$WWW/index.html" > "$STAGE/index.html"
grep -q "name=\"reva-canvas\" content=\"$CANVAS\"" "$STAGE/index.html" \
    || die "index.html has no reva-canvas meta tag to set"

cat > "$STAGE/README.txt" <<EOF
$SITE: Reva Forth in the browser (WebAssembly), as a static site.

Serve this folder with any static web server and open index.html:

  - on a web host: upload the zip, unzip it anywhere (a subfolder is fine),
    and open https://your.host/path/$SITE/
  - locally: python3 -m http.server -d $SITE 8000, then http://localhost:8000/
    (or run the reva-serve binary, which embeds the same files)

Opening index.html as a file:// URL does not work: browsers do not run
Web Workers or fetch files from file:// pages.

Files you write in Forth are kept in your browser's localStorage for this
site's origin (scheme, host and port): another host or port starts empty.

URL options: ?canvas=split|pane|window, ?package=DIR/ (another package
folder on the same site), ?include=FILE, ?eval=TEXT, ?image=FILE.

Licenses: LICENSE.txt (Reva, public domain), LICENSE-MIT.txt (the portable
core).$( [ -n "$PKG" ] && printf '\nThe package in pkg/ has its own terms; see its files.' )
EOF

# Reproducible: fixed timestamps (the last commit's, in UTC) and sorted names.
stamp=$(cd "$ROOT" && TZ=UTC git log -1 --format=%cd --date=format-local:%Y%m%d%H%M 2>/dev/null || true)
stamp=${stamp:-202601010000}
find "$STAGE" -exec env TZ=UTC touch -t "$stamp" {} +
(cd "$OUT" && find "$SITE" | LC_ALL=C sort | TZ=UTC zip -qX -@ "$ZIP")

n=$(find "$STAGE" -type f | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
size=$(wc -c < "$ZIP" | tr -d ' ')
echo "make-web-zip: $ZIP ($n files, $size bytes)"
echo "make-web-zip: site at $STAGE (try: python3 -m http.server -d $STAGE 8000)"

#!/bin/sh
# make-web-zip.sh: build the browser REPL as a static site and zip it, ready
# to upload to any web host, unzip, and serve as plain files.
#
#   scripts/make-web-zip.sh [options]          (from anywhere; POSIX sh)
#
#   --package DIR   include DIR (a folder with reva-package.json) as pkg/ and
#                   open it by default; its manifest must list its "files"
#   --name NAME     zip and folder name (default: reva, or the package's id)
#   --version V     version in the name (default: the workspace version)
#   --canvas MODE   default graphics placement: split (default), pane, window
#   --out DIR       where the zip goes (default: target/web)
#   --no-build      use the reva.wasm already in components/web/crates/reva-web/www
#
# Result: OUT/NAME-web-V.zip holding one folder NAME-web-V/ (the site) and
# the same tree unzipped at OUT/NAME-web-V/ (what reva-serve embeds).
#
# The site is static and relative: index.html, the JS modules, reva.wasm,
# canvas.html and, with a package, pkg/.  It needs no server logic, no
# special headers (no SharedArrayBuffer, so no COOP/COEP), and works under
# any subpath (https://host/some/dir/NAME-web-V/).  Files written by Forth
# are kept in the visitor's localStorage, which is per origin: a site moved
# to another host or port starts with no saved files.
#
# The zip is reproducible: files are listed in sorted order and stamped
# with the last commit's time (UTC), so the same commit gives the same zip.
set -eu
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd "$HERE/.." && pwd)
WWW=$ROOT/components/web/crates/reva-web/www
PKG= NAME= VERSION= CANVAS=split OUT=$ROOT/target/web BUILD=1

die() { echo "make-web-zip: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case $1 in
        --package) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "$1 needs a value"; PKG=$2; shift 2 ;;
        --name) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "$1 needs a value"; NAME=$2; shift 2 ;;
        --version) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "$1 needs a value"; VERSION=$2; shift 2 ;;
        --canvas) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "$1 needs a value"; CANVAS=$2; shift 2 ;;
        --out) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "$1 needs a value"; OUT=$2; shift 2 ;;
        --no-build) BUILD=; shift ;;
        -h|--help) sed -n '2,25p' "$0" | cut -c3-; exit 0 ;;
        *) die "unknown option $1 (try --help)" ;;
    esac
done
case $CANVAS in split|pane|window) ;; *) die "--canvas $CANVAS: use split, pane or window" ;; esac
command -v zip >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "needs zip (macOS has it; Debian/Ubuntu: apt install zip)"

if [ -n "$PKG" ]; then
    [ -f "$PKG/reva-package.json" ] || die "$PKG: no reva-package.json"
    PKG=$(cd "$PKG" && pwd)
    grep -q '"files"' "$PKG/reva-package.json" \
        || die "$PKG/reva-package.json has no \"files\" list (a static server cannot list a folder)"
    if [ -z "$NAME" ]; then
        # the manifest's "id", else the folder name
        NAME=$(tr -d '\n' < "$PKG/reva-package.json" | awk '{ if (match($0, /"id"[ \t]*:[ \t]*"[A-Za-z0-9._-]+"/)) { s = substr($0, RSTART, RLENGTH); sub(/.*"id"[ \t]*:[ \t]*"/, "", s); sub(/"$/, "", s); print s } }')
        [ -n "$NAME" ] || NAME=$(basename "$PKG")
    fi
fi
NAME=${NAME:-reva}
case $NAME in *[!A-Za-z0-9._-]*|'') die "--name $NAME: use letters, digits, . _ -" ;; esac
if [ -z "$VERSION" ]; then
    VERSION=$(awk -F'"' '/^version *=/ { print $2; exit }' "$ROOT/components/vm/Cargo.toml")
fi

[ -n "$BUILD" ] && "$HERE/build-web.sh" >/dev/null
[ -f "$WWW/reva.wasm" ] || die "no $WWW/reva.wasm (run without --no-build)"

SITE=$NAME-web-$VERSION
mkdir -p "$OUT"
OUT=$(cd "$OUT" && pwd)
STAGE=$OUT/$SITE
ZIP=$OUT/$SITE.zip
rm -rf "$STAGE" "$ZIP"
mkdir -p "$STAGE"
for f in index.html host.js reva.js reva-worker.js reva.wasm ui.js tui.js canvas.html split.js package.js about.js lineedit.js ansi.js sqlite.js store.js upload.js favicon.png favicon.ico; do
    cp "$WWW/$f" "$STAGE/$f"
done
cp -R "$WWW/ui" "$STAGE/ui"
cp "$ROOT/LICENSE" "$STAGE/LICENSE.txt"
cp "$ROOT/LICENSE-MIT" "$STAGE/LICENSE-MIT.txt"

# The page's defaults and the build stamp (About), as meta tags (index.html reads them when the URL
# has no ?package= or ?canvas=).
pkgmeta=
if [ -n "$PKG" ]; then
    mkdir -p "$STAGE/pkg"
    # every file of the package except dot files (.git and friends)
    (cd "$PKG" && find . -type f ! -path '*/.*' | while IFS= read -r f; do
        mkdir -p "$STAGE/pkg/$(dirname "$f")"
        cp "$f" "$STAGE/pkg/$f"
    done)
    pkgmeta=pkg/
fi
# A hash of the site's files (package included): a new build is new module
# URLs below, so browsers never mix stale modules with fresh ones, while an
# unchanged build stays cached.  The page fetches its other files with
# no-cache (reva.js FRESH).  POSIX cksum, files in a fixed order.
site=$(cd "$STAGE" && find . -type f | LC_ALL=C sort | xargs cat | cksum | cut -d' ' -f1)
build="$("$HERE/build-stamp.sh") $site"
awk -v pkg="$pkgmeta" -v canvas="$CANVAS" -v build="$build" '
    index($0, "<meta name=\"reva-package\" content=\"\">") { sub(/content=""/, "content=\"" pkg "\"") }
    index($0, "<meta name=\"reva-canvas\" content=\"\">") { sub(/content=""/, "content=\"" canvas "\"") }
    index($0, "<meta name=\"reva-build\" content=\"\">") { sub(/content=""/, "content=\"" build "\"") }
    { print }' "$WWW/index.html" > "$STAGE/index.html"
grep -q "name=\"reva-canvas\" content=\"$CANVAS\"" "$STAGE/index.html" \
    || die "index.html has no reva-canvas meta tag to set"

cat > "$STAGE/README.txt" <<EOF
$SITE: Reva Forth in the browser (WebAssembly), as a static site.

Serve this folder with any static web server and open index.html:

  - on a web host: upload the zip, unzip it anywhere (a subfolder is fine),
    and open https://your.host/path/$SITE/
  - locally: python3 -m http.server -d $SITE 8000, then http://localhost:8000/
    (or run the reva-serve binary, which embeds the same files)

Opening index.html as a file:// URL does not work: browsers do not run
Web Workers or fetch files from file:// pages.

Files you write in Forth are kept in your browser's localStorage for this
site's origin (scheme, host and port): another host or port starts empty.

URL options: ?canvas=split|pane|window, ?package=DIR/ (another package
folder on the same site), ?include=FILE, ?eval=TEXT, ?image=FILE.

Licenses: LICENSE.txt (Reva, public domain), LICENSE-MIT.txt (the portable
core).$( [ -n "$PKG" ] && printf '\nThe package in pkg/ has its own terms; see its files.' )
EOF

# Reproducible: fixed timestamps (the last commit's, in UTC) and sorted names.
stamp=$(cd "$ROOT" && TZ=UTC git log -1 --format=%cd --date=format-local:%Y%m%d%H%M 2>/dev/null || true)
stamp=${stamp:-202601010000}
find "$STAGE" -exec env TZ=UTC touch -t "$stamp" {} +
(cd "$OUT" && find "$SITE" | LC_ALL=C sort | TZ=UTC zip -qX -@ "$ZIP")

n=$(find "$STAGE" -type f | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
size=$(wc -c < "$ZIP" | tr -d ' ')
echo "make-web-zip: $ZIP ($n files, $size bytes)"
echo "make-web-zip: site at $STAGE (try: python3 -m http.server -d $STAGE 8000)"

#!/bin/sh
# make-web-zip.sh: build the browser REPL as a static site and zip it, ready
# to upload to any web host, unzip, and serve as plain files.
#
#   scripts/make-web-zip.sh [options]          (from anywhere; POSIX sh)
#
#   --package DIR   include DIR (a folder with reva-package.json) as pkg/ and
#                   open it by default; its manifest must list its "files"
#   --name NAME     zip and folder name (default: reva, or the package's id)
#   --version V     version in the name (default: the workspace version)
#   --canvas MODE   default graphics placement: split (default), pane, window
#   --out DIR       where the zip goes (default: target/web)
#   --no-build      use the reva.wasm already in components/web/crates/reva-web/www
#
# Result: OUT/NAME-web-V.zip holding one folder NAME-web-V/ (the site) and
# the same tree unzipped at OUT/NAME-web-V/ (what reva-serve embeds).
#
# The site is static and relative: index.html, the JS modules, reva.wasm,
# canvas.html and, with a package, pkg/.  It needs no server logic, no
# special headers (no SharedArrayBuffer, so no COOP/COEP), and works under
# any subpath (https://host/some/dir/NAME-web-V/).  Files written by Forth
# are kept in the visitor's localStorage, which is per origin: a site moved
# to another host or port starts with no saved files.
#
# The zip is reproducible: files are listed in sorted order and stamped
# with the last commit's time (UTC), so the same commit gives the same zip.
set -eu
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd "$HERE/.." && pwd)
WWW=$ROOT/components/web/crates/reva-web/www
PKG= NAME= VERSION= CANVAS=split OUT=$ROOT/target/web BUILD=1

die() { echo "make-web-zip: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case $1 in
        --package) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "$1 needs a value"; PKG=$2; shift 2 ;;
        --name) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "$1 needs a value"; NAME=$2; shift 2 ;;
        --version) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "$1 needs a value"; VERSION=$2; shift 2 ;;
        --canvas) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "$1 needs a value"; CANVAS=$2; shift 2 ;;
        --out) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "$1 needs a value"; OUT=$2; shift 2 ;;
        --no-build) BUILD=; shift ;;
        -h|--help) sed -n '2,25p' "$0" | cut -c3-; exit 0 ;;
        *) die "unknown option $1 (try --help)" ;;
    esac
done
case $CANVAS in split|pane|window) ;; *) die "--canvas $CANVAS: use split, pane or window" ;; esac
command -v zip >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "needs zip (macOS has it; Debian/Ubuntu: apt install zip)"

if [ -n "$PKG" ]; then
    [ -f "$PKG/reva-package.json" ] || die "$PKG: no reva-package.json"
    PKG=$(cd "$PKG" && pwd)
    grep -q '"files"' "$PKG/reva-package.json" \
        || die "$PKG/reva-package.json has no \"files\" list (a static server cannot list a folder)"
    if [ -z "$NAME" ]; then
        # the manifest's "id", else the folder name
        NAME=$(tr -d '\n' < "$PKG/reva-package.json" | awk '{ if (match($0, /"id"[ \t]*:[ \t]*"[A-Za-z0-9._-]+"/)) { s = substr($0, RSTART, RLENGTH); sub(/.*"id"[ \t]*:[ \t]*"/, "", s); sub(/"$/, "", s); print s } }')
        [ -n "$NAME" ] || NAME=$(basename "$PKG")
    fi
fi
NAME=${NAME:-reva}
case $NAME in *[!A-Za-z0-9._-]*|'') die "--name $NAME: use letters, digits, . _ -" ;; esac
if [ -z "$VERSION" ]; then
    VERSION=$(awk -F'"' '/^version *=/ { print $2; exit }' "$ROOT/components/vm/Cargo.toml")
fi

[ -n "$BUILD" ] && "$HERE/build-web.sh" >/dev/null
[ -f "$WWW/reva.wasm" ] || die "no $WWW/reva.wasm (run without --no-build)"

SITE=$NAME-web-$VERSION
mkdir -p "$OUT"
OUT=$(cd "$OUT" && pwd)
STAGE=$OUT/$SITE
ZIP=$OUT/$SITE.zip
rm -rf "$STAGE" "$ZIP"
mkdir -p "$STAGE"
for f in index.html host.js reva.js reva-worker.js reva.wasm ui.js tui.js canvas.html split.js package.js about.js lineedit.js ansi.js sqlite.js store.js upload.js favicon.png favicon.ico; do
    cp "$WWW/$f" "$STAGE/$f"
done
cp -R "$WWW/ui" "$STAGE/ui"
cp "$ROOT/LICENSE" "$STAGE/LICENSE.txt"
cp "$ROOT/LICENSE-MIT" "$STAGE/LICENSE-MIT.txt"

# The page's defaults and the build stamp (About), as meta tags (index.html reads them when the URL
# has no ?package= or ?canvas=).
pkgmeta=
if [ -n "$PKG" ]; then
    mkdir -p "$STAGE/pkg"
    # every file of the package except dot files (.git and friends)
    (cd "$PKG" && find . -type f ! -path '*/.*' | while IFS= read -r f; do
        mkdir -p "$STAGE/pkg/$(dirname "$f")"
        cp "$f" "$STAGE/pkg/$f"
    done)
    pkgmeta=pkg/
fi
# A hash of the site's files (package included): a new build is new module
# URLs below, so browsers never mix stale modules with fresh ones, while an
# unchanged build stays cached.  The page fetches its other files with
# no-cache (reva.js FRESH).  POSIX cksum, files in a fixed order.
site=$(cd "$STAGE" && find . -type f | LC_ALL=C sort | xargs cat | cksum | cut -d' ' -f1)
build="$("$HERE/build-stamp.sh") $site"
awk -v pkg="$pkgmeta" -v canvas="$CANVAS" -v build="$build" '
    index($0, "<meta name=\"reva-package\" content=\"\">") { sub(/content=""/, "content=\"" pkg "\"") }
    index($0, "<meta name=\"reva-canvas\" content=\"\">") { sub(/content=""/, "content=\"" canvas "\"") }
    index($0, "<meta name=\"reva-build\" content=\"\">") { sub(/content=""/, "content=\"" build "\"") }
    { print }' "$WWW/index.html" > "$STAGE/index.html"
grep -q "name=\"reva-canvas\" content=\"$CANVAS\"" "$STAGE/index.html" \
    || die "index.html has no reva-canvas meta tag to set"
# Every module and worker URL ("./x.js"), and the UI's wasm, carry ?v=SITE.
for f in "$STAGE"/*.js "$STAGE"/ui/*.js "$STAGE/index.html"; do
    sed-rs -i -e "s#(\"\\./[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\\.js)\"#\\1?v=$site\"#g" \
        -e "s#'(reva_ui_web_bg\\.wasm)'#'\\1?v=$site'#g" "$f" || die "$f: could not stamp module URLs"
done
grep -q "\"./reva.js?v=$site\"" "$STAGE/index.html" || die "index.html: module URLs not stamped"

cat > "$STAGE/README.txt" <<EOF
$SITE: Reva Forth in the browser (WebAssembly), as a static site.

Serve this folder with any static web server and open index.html:

  - on a web host: upload the zip, unzip it anywhere (a subfolder is fine),
    and open https://your.host/path/$SITE/
  - locally: python3 -m http.server -d $SITE 8000, then http://localhost:8000/
    (or run the reva-serve binary, which embeds the same files)

Opening index.html as a file:// URL does not work: browsers do not run
Web Workers or fetch files from file:// pages.

Files you write in Forth are kept in your browser's localStorage for this
site's origin (scheme, host and port): another host or port starts empty.

URL options: ?canvas=split|pane|window, ?package=DIR/ (another package
folder on the same site), ?include=FILE, ?eval=TEXT, ?image=FILE.

Licenses: LICENSE.txt (Reva, public domain), LICENSE-MIT.txt (the portable
core).$( [ -n "$PKG" ] && printf '\nThe package in pkg/ has its own terms; see its files.' )
EOF

# Reproducible: fixed timestamps (the last commit's, in UTC) and sorted names.
stamp=$(cd "$ROOT" && TZ=UTC git log -1 --format=%cd --date=format-local:%Y%m%d%H%M 2>/dev/null || true)
stamp=${stamp:-202601010000}
find "$STAGE" -exec env TZ=UTC touch -t "$stamp" {} +
(cd "$OUT" && find "$SITE" | LC_ALL=C sort | TZ=UTC zip -qX -@ "$ZIP")

n=$(find "$STAGE" -type f | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
size=$(wc -c < "$ZIP" | tr -d ' ')
echo "make-web-zip: $ZIP ($n files, $size bytes)"
echo "make-web-zip: site at $STAGE (try: python3 -m http.server -d $STAGE 8000)"

content.content:
## The uploadable zip: `just web-zip`

`scripts/make-web-zip.sh` (POSIX sh; `just web-zip` runs it) builds
`reva.wasm` and writes `target/web/NAME-web-VERSION.zip`, holding one
folder `NAME-web-VERSION/`:

```text
index.html  reva.js  reva-worker.js  reva.wasm  host.js  ui.js  canvas.html
split.js  package.js  README.txt  LICENSE.txt  LICENSE-MIT.txt  [pkg/ ...]
```

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--package DIR` | copy DIR into `pkg/` and open it by default; NAME defaults to its `id` |
| `--canvas MODE` | the default graphics placement (default `split`) |
| `--name NAME`, `--version V` | the zip's name (default `reva`, the workspace version) |
| `--out DIR` | where the zip goes (default `target/web`) |
| `--no-build` | use the `reva.wasm` already built |

With `just`: `just web-zip --package path/to/pkg`. CoSy's zip is built in
its own repository (`just cosy-zip` in ba-cosy-zip-fork), which calls this
script.

To check a zip the way a web host serves it, unzip it into a subdirectory
of any static server:

```text
mkdir -p /tmp/site/a/b && cd /tmp/site/a/b && unzip ~/reva-web-VERSION.zip
python3 -m http.server -d /tmp/site 8000
#   open http://localhost:8000/a/b/reva-web-VERSION/
```

`file://` does not work: browsers do not start module workers or fetch
files from `file://` pages. To run the same tree with no server at all,
use [reva-serve](serve.md), which embeds it in one binary.

## The live demo: `just publish`

folder at the same address used to keep running old files. Static hosts

  and an unchanged one stays cached.

  when that is newer. So a package rebuilt at the same reva-fork commit
  gets newer times, and servers that answer by Last-Modified send the new
  `index.html`.
- The About dialog shows the build's commit, date and site hash, so a
  stale page is easy to tell.

[reva-serve](serve.md) sends `Cache-Control: no-cache` for everything.

#!/bin/sh
# build-serve.sh: build reva-serve, the one-binary local web app, for
# release: the static site (make-web-zip.sh) embedded in a small server.
#
#   scripts/build-serve.sh [options] [TARGET ...]        (POSIX sh)
#
#   --site DIR      embed DIR (a site tree, e.g. from make-web-zip.sh)
#                   instead of building one
#   --package DIR   build the site with this package (make-web-zip.sh --package)
#   --name NAME     app name: binary NAME-serve (default: reva, or the package id)
#   --port N        preferred port (default 8421)
#   --out DIR       where binaries go (default: target/serve)
#   --no-build      do not rebuild reva.wasm
#
# TARGET is a Rust target triple, or one of these shorthands:
#   mac      universal macOS binary (arm64 + x86_64, joined with lipo; macOS only)
#   linux    static Linux binary for this machine's CPU (x86_64/aarch64 musl)
#   windows  x86_64-pc-windows-gnu (needs mingw-w64 when not on Windows)
# Default: mac on macOS, linux on Linux, the host triple elsewhere.
#
# Output: OUT/NAME-serve-VERSION-TARGET[.exe], plus a .sha256 beside each.
# Targets are added with `rustup target add` as needed.  The binary has no
# crate dependencies (std only), so any target rustup has will do.
set -eu
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd "$HERE/.." && pwd)
SITE= PKG= NAME= PORT=8421 OUT=$ROOT/target/serve NOBUILD=
die() { echo "build-serve: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case $1 in
        --site) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "$1 needs a value"; SITE=$2; shift 2 ;;
        --package) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "$1 needs a value"; PKG=$2; shift 2 ;;
        --name) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "$1 needs a value"; NAME=$2; shift 2 ;;
        --port) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "$1 needs a value"; PORT=$2; shift 2 ;;
        --out) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "$1 needs a value"; OUT=$2; shift 2 ;;
        --no-build) NOBUILD=--no-build; shift ;;
        -h|--help) sed -n '2,24p' "$0" | cut -c3-; exit 0 ;;
        -*) die "unknown option $1 (try --help)" ;;
        *) break ;;
    esac
done
VERSION=$(tr -d ' \n' < "$ROOT/VERSION")

# The site: given, or built the way the uploadable zip is.
if [ -z "$SITE" ]; then
    zipargs="--out $ROOT/target/web $NOBUILD"
    [ -n "$PKG" ] && zipargs="$zipargs --package $PKG"
    [ -n "$NAME" ] && zipargs="$zipargs --name $NAME"
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086 # word splitting is wanted (paths without spaces)
    line=$("$HERE/make-web-zip.sh" $zipargs | head -1)
    zip=${line#make-web-zip: }
    SITE=${zip%%.zip *}
    # pick up the name make-web-zip chose (the package id)
    base=$(basename "$SITE")
    NAME=${NAME:-${base%-web-*}}
fi
[ -f "$SITE/index.html" ] || die "$SITE: no index.html"
SITE=$(cd "$SITE" && pwd)
NAME=${NAME:-reva}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The gate: everything that must pass before a commit (`just check`).
#
#   scripts/check.sh            all of it
#   scripts/check.sh --fast     skip the desktop component (Tauri)
#
# Runs, and stops at the first failure:
#   1. every component (components/*, one Cargo workspace each) but the
#      desktop: cargo fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, tests (release);
#      and every component on the same version
#   2. the WebAssembly build and its node tests
#   3. components/desktop: cargo fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, tests
#   4. the reg-rs goldens on the release CLI; a failure is accepted only
#      if KNOWN_FAILURES lists it for this OS
#   5. the license check
#   6. sw-checklist: its FAIL count may not exceed SW_CHECKLIST_MAX_FAILS
#
# Bash 3.2 compatible (macOS /bin/bash).
set -euo pipefail
root="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"

# Goldens known to fail, per OS, until the step that fixes them
# (.agentrail: local-portable-gates).  The list may only shrink.
case "$(uname)" in
    Darwin) KNOWN_FAILURES="docs-samples" ;;
    *)      KNOWN_FAILURES="" ;;
esac

# sw-checklist FAILs: 51 on 2026-10-26, 49 after edition 2024, 47 after
# the web checks, 46 after the split of reva-vm, 40 after the word
# families (local-comp-words), 27 after vx86 (local-comp-x86), 22 after the
# machine (local-comp-core), 18 after the host (local-comp-host), 15 after
# vlib (local-comp-vlib), 7 after the CLI (local-comp-cli), 0 after the
# front ends (local-comp-front-ends).  It stays 0: the checklist is required.
SW_CHECKLIST_MAX_FAILS=0

fast=0
[[ "${1:-}" == --fast ]] && fast=1

step() { printf '\n== %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\ncheck: FAILED: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }

# The components the core builds from, dependencies first; the desktop
# (Tauri, a few hundred crates) is step 3.
COMPONENTS="macros x86-types x86-decode x86-alu x86-exec x86 host-base vfs host core-parts canvas ui ui-layout ui-grid ui-web core core-run iup vlib words-base words-interp words-dict words-os words vm sqlite cli-edit cli-host cli web serve"

version() { awk -F'"' '/^version *=/ { print $2; exit }' "$root/components/$1/Cargo.toml"; }
for c in $COMPONENTS; do
    step "components/$c: fmt, clippy, tests"
    (cd "$root/components/$c" && cargo fmt --check) || fail "$c: cargo fmt --check (run cargo fmt in components/$c)"
    (cd "$root/components/$c" && cargo clippy -q --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings) || fail "$c: clippy"
    (cd "$root/components/$c" && cargo test -q --release --workspace) || fail "$c: tests"
    [[ "$(version "$c")" == "$(version vm)" ]] || fail "$c: version $(version "$c"), not $(version vm) as components/vm"
done

step "web: wasm build, node tests"
"$root/scripts/build-web.sh" >/dev/null || fail "web: build-web.sh"
for t in smoke lineedit ansi store; do
    node "$root/components/web/crates/reva-web/test/$t.mjs" >/dev/null || fail "web: test/$t.mjs (run it for details)"
done

if [[ $fast -eq 0 ]]; then
    step "desktop: fmt, clippy, tests"
    (cd "$root/components/desktop" && cargo fmt --check) || fail "desktop: cargo fmt --check"
    "$root/components/desktop/build.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "desktop: build.sh (run it for details)"
    (cd "$root/components/desktop" && cargo clippy -q --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings) || fail "desktop: clippy"
    (cd "$root/components/desktop" && cargo test -q --workspace) || fail "desktop: tests"
fi

step "goldens (reg-rs, release CLI)"
out=$(cd "$root" && REVA=target/release/reva scripts/regress.sh 2>&1) || true
echo "$out" | grep -E 'passed|FAIL' || fail "goldens: no summary from regress.sh"
unexpected=""
for t in $(echo "$out" | sed -n 's/^ *FAIL: *//p'); do
    case " $KNOWN_FAILURES " in
        *" $t "*) echo "   (known failure on $(uname): $t)" ;;
        *)        unexpected="$unexpected $t" ;;
    esac
done
[[ -z "$unexpected" ]] || fail "goldens:$unexpected (details: REVA=target/release/reva scripts/regress.sh -v -p NAME)"

step "licenses"
"$root/scripts/license-check.sh" || fail "license-check.sh"

step "sw-checklist"
# sw-checklist exits 1 while it has FAILs; the count below is the test.
summary=$(cd "$root" && { sw-checklist 2>&1 || true; } | grep '^Summary:') || fail "sw-checklist did not run"
echo "$summary"
fails=$(echo "$summary" | sed -n 's/.* \([0-9][0-9]*\) failed.*/\1/p')
[[ -n "$fails" ]] || fail "sw-checklist: cannot read the FAIL count"
[[ "$fails" -le "$SW_CHECKLIST_MAX_FAILS" ]] ||
    fail "sw-checklist: $fails FAILs, more than $SW_CHECKLIST_MAX_FAILS (sw-checklist -v | grep FAIL)"

printf '\ncheck: ok\n'

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the Reva desktop app.
#
#   components/desktop/build.sh            build target/release/reva-desktop
#   components/desktop/build.sh --install  ... and install it as `reva-desktop` (cargo install)
#   components/desktop/build.sh --bundle   ... and make installers (.deb/.rpm, .app/.dmg; needs tauri-cli)
#
# Steps: build the WebAssembly VM (scripts/build-web.sh), assemble the
# page into components/desktop/dist (the browser page, with components/desktop/host.js in place of
# the browser's), then compile the native shell, which embeds dist.
# Linux needs WebKitGTK 4.1 headers (Debian/Ubuntu: libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev);
# macOS needs only Xcode's command line tools.
set -euo pipefail
here="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
"$here/../../scripts/build-web.sh" >/dev/null
www="$here/../web/crates/reva-web/www"
rm -rf "$here/dist" && mkdir -p "$here/dist"
cp "$www/index.html" "$www/reva.js" "$www/reva-worker.js" "$www/reva.wasm" \
   "$www/ui.js" "$www/tui.js" "$www/canvas.html" "$www/split.js" "$www/package.js" "$www/about.js" "$www/lineedit.js" "$www/ansi.js" "$www/sqlite.js" "$www/store.js" "$www/upload.js" "$www/favicon.png" "$here/dist/"
# the build stamp for the About dialog (reva-build meta tag)
stamp=$("$here/../../scripts/build-stamp.sh")
awk -v build="$stamp" '
    index($0, "<meta name=\"reva-build\" content=\"\">") { sub(/content=""/, "content=\"" build "\"") }
    { print }' "$www/index.html" > "$here/dist/index.html"
cp "$here/host.js" "$here/dist/host.js"
rm -rf "$here/dist/ui" && cp -R "$www/ui" "$here/dist/ui"
cd "$here"
case "${1:-}" in
    --install) cargo install --locked --path crates/reva-desktop ;;
    --bundle)  (cd crates/reva-desktop && cargo tauri build) ;;
    *)         cargo build --release ;;
esac
[[ "${1:-}" == --install ]] || echo "built: $(cd "$here/../.." && pwd)/target/release/reva-desktop"

### 19. Pasting several lines into the web REPL runs them as one (medium)

- **Symptom:** the web page's REPL input is `<input id="line">`
  (index.html, lineedit.js), a single-line box, so a paste of several
  lines turns each newline into a space and Enter sends one line. Forth
  then sees the lines run together, and the first `|` comment hides
  everything after it. Seen in the CoSy zip (2026.1102.0, served
  locally): six pasted lines ran as one, only the first two commands
  ran, and an object was left on the stack (`(1) 36DC28`). Copying
  examples from a README, a chat or a notebook is how people try CoSy,
  and the examples have `|` comments.
- **Repro:** open the web page, paste
  ```
  1 2 +  .   | three
  4 5 *  .   | twenty
  ```
  and press Enter: it prints `3` only. In the CLI (the lines on stdin)
  the same lines print `3 20`; the desktop app is not checked.
- **Workaround:** paste one line at a time; join lines by hand without
  `|` comments; or upload the lines as a file and run it (CoSy's
  `demo FILE`).
- **Suggested fix:** handle `paste` on the input: if the text has
  newlines, prevent the default and feed each line to the VM in turn, as
  if typed and Entered (echoing each, so the output reads like a
  session), keeping a trailing partial line in the box. A long paste
  should go through the same queue as typed lines, so the runaway guard
  (#81) and Stop still apply between lines. Optionally, Shift-Enter or a
  multi-line mode (a `<textarea>` that grows) for editing several lines
  before running them.

## CoSy-side issues (not for reva-fork)

These are in Bob's sources or data and are left as they are:

- **Old examples:** the `examples` text in `CoSy.csy` uses `^+` and
  `i^`, and `tstScript` uses `^eval`. These words are not in the current
  sources.
- **ForthDay15.csy:** its `script0` uses `"m`, which no longer exists, so
  restoring it prints `unknown word: "m` (harmless).
- **SaveRestoreMeta.f:** it is not loaded by CoSy.f, and loading it fails

content.content:
## Web page, desktop app, zips, `reva-serve`

All of these run the same page (`components/web/crates/reva-web/www/index.html`), whose
input line gets the keys from `www/lineedit.js`.

* **History** is in `localStorage`, one list per package: `reva:history`
  for plain Reva, `reva:<package id>:history` for a package (CoSy:
  `reva:cosy:history`), at most 1000 entries.  Blank lines and a repeat of
  the last entry are not added.  The list is re-read before each add, so
  two tabs add to one list rather than overwrite each other.
* **Browser-reserved keys.**  In a browser tab, Chrome and Firefox keep
  Ctrl-W (close tab), Ctrl-N (new window) and Ctrl-T (new tab) for
  themselves; use Alt-Backspace and Down instead.  In the desktop app every
  key reaches the line.  Ctrl-R is taken from the browser's reload while
  the input has focus, and Ctrl-X from cut (Shift-Delete still cuts; on
  a Mac cut is Cmd-X).
* **Ctrl-C** stops a running word (as before); while searching it ends the
  search instead.
* On macOS, Alt-B/F/D work whatever character Option would type, and
  Cmd-key shortcuts are left to the system.

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# The REPL: history and line editing

Every Reva REPL keeps a history of the lines typed at `ok>` and edits the
current line with Emacs keys (the readline/bash defaults).  This page is
the key table both front ends follow.

| Keys | What it does |
|------|--------------|
| Up / Down, Ctrl-P / Ctrl-N | previous / next history entry (Down past the newest brings back the line you were typing) |
| Ctrl-R / Ctrl-S | search history backward / forward; type to narrow, press again for the next match |
| Enter (while searching) | run the match |
| Esc, Ctrl-G, Ctrl-C (while searching) | give up, put the line back |
| any other key (while searching) | keep the match on the line, then do that key's usual thing |
| Ctrl-A / Ctrl-E | start / end of line |
| Ctrl-B / Ctrl-F | back / forward a character |
| Alt-B / Alt-F | back / forward a word |
| Ctrl-D, Ctrl-H | delete the character under / before the cursor |
| Ctrl-K / Ctrl-U | kill to end / start of line |
| Ctrl-W, Alt-Backspace | kill the word before the cursor |
| Alt-D | kill the word after the cursor |
| Ctrl-Y | yank (paste) the last kill |
| Ctrl-T | transpose characters |
| Ctrl-X Ctrl-E | run the line, as Enter does (Emacs's chord; it evaluates a line in the notebook too); any other key after Ctrl-X is itself |
| Ctrl-L | clear the screen (CLI only) |
| Ctrl-C | CLI: drop the line, new prompt (while a word runs: ends `reva`, as before); web: stop the running word |
| Ctrl-D on an empty line | CLI: end of input (`reva` exits 0) |

## Command line: `reva`

* **Only at a terminal.**  When stdin is a terminal, `reva` reads each line
  through its own small editor (components cli-edit and cli-host: reva-lineedit, reva-term; `scripts/pty-lineedit.py` drives it at a pseudo-terminal in the regression suite).
  Piped or redirected input is read as before, byte for byte, so scripts
  and the reg-rs goldens see no change.
* **History file:** `$REVA_HISTORY` if set (set it empty for no file),
  else `~/.reva_history` (`%USERPROFILE%\.reva_history` on Windows).
  Each line is appended as it is entered, so history survives `bye`,
  `restart`, a crash and `run-cosy`'s restart loop.  1000 entries are kept;
  the file is trimmed when it grows past 2000.  CoSy's `run-cosy` uses
  `~/.cosy_history`, so CoSy and plain Reva keep separate histories.
* **Off switches:** `reva --no-edit`, or `TERM=dumb`, reads plain lines
  (the terminal's own editing only).  If the terminal cannot be put in raw
  mode (for example Git Bash's mintty), `reva` falls back to plain lines
  by itself.
* Long lines scroll sideways on one row instead of wrapping.
* **Colour listings:** `pp FILE` (after `needs highlight/core`) lists
  source in colour; see [highlight.md](highlight.md) and `reva --color`.
* If the terminal is ever left in a strange state, `stty sane` (Unix)
  puts it right; `reva` restores it after each line and on a panic.

## Web page, desktop app, zips, `reva-serve`

All of these run the same page (`components/web/crates/reva-web/www/index.html`), whose
input line gets the keys from `www/lineedit.js`.

* **History** is in `localStorage`, one list per package: `reva:history`
  for plain Reva, `reva:<package id>:history` for a package (CoSy:
  `reva:cosy:history`), at most 1000 entries.  Blank lines and a repeat of
  the last entry are not added.  The list is re-read before each add, so
  two tabs add to one list rather than overwrite each other.
* **Browser-reserved keys.**  In a browser tab, Chrome and Firefox keep
  Ctrl-W (close tab), Ctrl-N (new window) and Ctrl-T (new tab) for
  themselves; use Alt-Backspace and Down instead.  In the desktop app every
  key reaches the line.  Ctrl-R is taken from the browser's reload while
  the input has focus, and Ctrl-X from cut (Shift-Delete still cuts; on
  a Mac cut is Cmd-X).
* **Ctrl-C** stops a running word (as before); while searching it ends the
  search instead.
* On macOS, Alt-B/F/D work whatever character Option would type, and
  Cmd-key shortcuts are left to the system.

## Help: `help WORD`, `help/ TEXT`

At any prompt (CLI, web page, desktop app), `help WORD` shows a word's
documentation: its stack picture, context, source and description, as
the original Reva's help did. `help/ TEXT` lists the documented words
whose names contain TEXT, and `help` alone says how to use both.

```text
ok> help dup
dup  ( a -- a a )
  context: ~   source: src/reva.f
  Duplicate the top stack item
```

The original read a SQLite database (`help.db`, built by
`tools/genhelp.f`). reva-fork builds a text index of the same
documentation, `src/help.txt` and the `def:` entries after the `|||` line
of every file in `lib/`, when it is built (reva-embedded's `helpgen.rs`),
and embeds it as `/reva/lib/help.idx`; `lib/helper` reads it. So help
needs no SQLite and covers new libraries as soon as they document their
words. The golden `help-content` checks real descriptions and that every
documented word (1377) is found; the web smoke test checks help in the
browser build.

## Design

* **Line level, in the host.**  The VM reads whole lines: the page feeds a
  line on Enter, and the CLI hands over a line once it is edited, as a
  terminal in canonical mode always did.  So `KEY`, `ACCEPT` and `REFILL`
  are untouched (`KEY` gets the next character of the entered line), and
  editing needs no VM support.  Lines typed for `KEY` are recorded in the
  history like any other.
* **Raw mode only while editing.**  The CLI switches the terminal to raw
  mode when it starts reading a line and back before Forth runs, so
  program output, Ctrl-C during a run and exits behave as before.
* **No crates.**  rustyline and similar crates would add a dozen
  dependencies to review for licenses (`scripts/license-check.sh`).  The
  editor is about 500 lines with unit tests; Unix raw mode uses the C
  library's `tcgetattr`/`cfmakeraw`/`tcsetattr` through an opaque buffer
  (no `struct termios` layout to get wrong per platform), Windows uses
  `SetConsoleMode` with virtual terminal input.
* **Small and dependency-free.**  `lineedit.js` is one module: pure editing
  operations (`edit`), a key map (`keyCommand`), the `History` list, and
  `lineEditor(input, …)` which joins them to the element.  The pure parts
  are tested in Node: `node components/web/crates/reva-web/test/lineedit.mjs` (in `just
  test`).  The CLI's decoder, editor, search and history have unit tests
  (`cargo test -p reva-cli`).
* **Never in the way.**  Storage errors (full, blocked, private mode) leave
  history in memory for the session; a broken stored value reads as empty.

      ['] nb-cx z" K_cX" set-callback
      ['] nb-ce z" K_cE" set-callback
      ['] nb-any z" K_ANY" set-callback
      ['] nb-f1 z" K_F1" set-callback

: notebook ( -- )  nb-dialog nb-load show gui-main-loop nb-save destroy ;

| vim: ft=reva :
|
| ui/notebook -- a small notebook in the TUI (reva-fork; docs/ui-model.md)
|
|   needs ui/notebook  notebook
|
| Type a Forth line in the top pane and press Ctrl-J or F6 (fn+F6 on a
| Mac keyboard): the line under the cursor is evaluated, and what it prints,
| any error and the stack it leaves show in the lower pane.  Enter starts
| a new line, Tab moves between the panes and the Done button, Done or
| the x in the top border closes it.  It fills the window, and keeps the
| top pane's text in notebook.txt (in the current folder: the desktop
| app's, the browser's saved files), loaded when it opens and saved at
| each evaluation.  F1 shows all the keys.

push~

needs ui/gui

~
with~ ~ui

variable nb-text   variable nb-res   variable nb-status

| The line under the cursor of the top pane.
: nb-line ( -- a n )  nb-text @ caret-y? line-text? rot drop ;

| While a line is evaluated, what it prints goes to the lower pane.
| `attr` makes its strings C strings in place (a 0 after them), so what
| is typed (word names in the dictionary, for `words`) is copied first.
variable nb-old-emit   variable nb-old-type   variable nb-emit-pad
create nb-buf 256 allot
: nb-chunk ( a n -- )  >r nb-buf r@ move  nb-res @ nb-buf r> " INSERT" attr drop ;
: nb-type ( a n -- )
  repeat
    2dup 255 min dup >r nb-chunk
    swap r@ + swap r> -
  dup 0 > while 2drop ;
: nb-emit ( c -- )  nb-emit-pad c!  nb-emit-pad 1 nb-type ;
: nb-to-pane ( -- )
  ['] emit @ nb-old-emit !  ['] type @ nb-old-type !
  ['] nb-emit is emit  ['] nb-type is type ;
: nb-to-repl ( -- )  nb-old-emit @ is emit  nb-old-type @ is type ;

| What the line left on the stack, oldest first (what is above depth d0).
variable nb-d0
: nb-.new ( -- )
  depth nb-d0 @ - dup 0 > if dup 0 do dup i - pick . loop then drop ;

| The top pane's text is kept in notebook.txt: saved at every evaluation
| and when the notebook closes; what was there when it opened is copied
| to notebook.bak first, so a bad session can be undone.
| notebook-file ( a n -- ) names another file (a package's own notebook
| beside Reva's); its backup is the same name with .bak for .txt.
create nb-name 256 allot  " notebook.txt" nb-name place
create nb-bakname 260 allot
: nb-file ( -- a n )  nb-name count ;
: notebook-file ( a n -- )  255 min nb-name place ;
: nb-bak ( -- a n )
  nb-file dup 4 >if 2dup + 4 - 4 " .txt" cmp 0if 4 - then then  nb-bakname place
  " .bak" nb-bakname +place  nb-bakname count ;
: nb-write ( a n file n2 -- )  creat >r r@ write r> close ;
: nb-save ( -- )  nb-text @ getval rot drop  nb-file nb-write ;

| F6: evaluate the line; its output, any error and the stack below; then
| save.  A plain word, not a `callback` one: the TUI runs it on the data
| stack (as IUP called C callbacks) and puts the stack back afterwards, so
| words like `help` and `.s` work as at the REPL.
: nb-f6
  nb-res @ " " setval drop
  depth nb-d0 !
  nb-to-pane
  nb-line ['] eval catch ?dup if ." error " . cr then
  cr ." stack: " nb-.new
  nb-to-repl
  nb-res @ " 1,1" " CARET" attr drop
  nb-status @ " evaluated" title drop
  nb-save
  gui-default ;

| Ctrl-X Ctrl-E: evaluate, as in Emacs (and the REPLs); Ctrl-E alone is
| still the end of the line, and any other key after Ctrl-X is itself.
variable nb-prefix
: nb-cx ( -- n )  nb-prefix on gui-ignore ;
: nb-ce ( -- n )  nb-prefix @ if nb-prefix off nb-f6 else gui-default then ;
: nb-any ( -- n )  nb-prefix off gui-default ;

| F1: what the keys do, in the lower pane.
: nb-.help ( -- )
  ." Ctrl-J, Ctrl-X Ctrl-E, F6 (fn+F6 on a Mac), Cmd-Enter: evaluate the" cr
  ."        line; what it prints, any error and the stack show here" cr
  ." Enter  a new line; arrows, Home, End, Ctrl-A, Ctrl-E, Ctrl-K edit" cr
  ." Cmd-V  paste (Ctrl-V elsewhere)     Tab  the next pane or button" cr
  ." Cmd-Z  undo (Ctrl-Z elsewhere)      Ctrl-Y  redo" cr
  ." Done   or the x in the top border: close.  Saved in notebook.txt at" cr
  ."        each evaluation and on closing; notebook.bak: as it was opened" cr
  ." Forth needs a space between words: 6 7 *  not  6 7*" ;
: nb-f1
  nb-res @ " " setval drop
  nb-to-pane nb-.help nb-to-repl
  nb-res @ " 1,1" " CARET" attr drop
  gui-default ;

: nb-dialog ( -- dialog )
  dialog[
    " Ctrl-J or F6 evaluates the line  -  F1 help  -  Done closes" label[ expand-horizontal dup nb-status ! ]w
    editbox[ expand
      ['] nb-f6 z" K_F6" set-callback
      ['] nb-f6 z" K_cCR" set-callback
      ['] nb-f6 z" K_cJ" set-callback
      ['] nb-cx z" K_cX" set-callback
      ['] nb-ce z" K_cE" set-callback
      ['] nb-any z" K_ANY" set-callback
      ['] nb-f1 z" K_F1" set-callback
      dup nb-text ! ]w
    editbox[ " x64" size expand-horizontal dup nb-res ! ]w
    hbox[ " Done" button[ { gui-close } action ]w ]w
  ]d " FULLxFULL" size " Reva notebook" title ;

| A first notebook (no file yet) starts with lines to try: nb-examples,
| deferred, so a package can give its own (each line by notebook-line).
: nb-line+ ( a n -- )  nb-text @ -rot " APPEND" attr drop ;
: notebook-line ( a n -- )  nb-line+ ;
: nb-reva-examples ( -- )
  " | Put the cursor on a line and press Ctrl-J (or F6).  F1: help." nb-line+
  " 2 3 +" nb-line+
  " 6 7 * dup . 1+" nb-line+
  " : sq dup * ;  7 sq" nb-line+
  " : tens  10 0 do i 10 * . loop ;  tens" nb-line+
  " words" nb-line+
  nb-text @ " 2,1" " CARET" attr drop ;
defer nb-examples  ' nb-reva-examples is nb-examples
| Load the file (copied to its backup first), or the examples.
: nb-load ( -- )
  nb-file slurp dup 0if 2drop nb-examples ;then
  2dup nb-bak nb-write  nb-text @ -rot setval drop ;

| Open the notebook; it returns when the notebook is closed.
: notebook ( -- )  nb-dialog nb-load show gui-main-loop nb-save destroy ;

pop~

content.content:
### 20. The web zip's ?v= stamp breaks the TUI's wasm import (high)

- **Symptom:** since reva-fork #83 ("A rebuilt web site is never run
  stale", which answers ask 16), a web zip built from `dev` cannot load
  the TUI: `go` (and any TUI) prints `*** the TUI could not be loaded:
  WebAssembly.instantiate(): Import #0 "./reva_ui_web_bg.js": module is
  not an object or function`, and the page logs the same TypeError.
  CoSy's check-web fails "go opens Bob's Tui.f window" and "no page
  errors"; the same checks pass on a zip built before #83.
- **Cause:** `scripts/make-web-zip.sh` adds `?v=SITE` to every quoted
  `"./x.js"` in `ui/*.js`. In wasm-bindgen's `ui/reva_ui_web.js` one of
  them is not a URL but the wasm's import module name, the key of the
  imports object (`"./reva_ui_web_bg.js": import0,` at line 480 of the
  `www/ui` build). Stamped, the key no longer matches the name the wasm
  imports.
- **Repro:** `REVA_FORK=../reva-fork sh reva-fork-subset/check-web.sh`
  here, against reva-fork `dev` 56e5b02; or build any web zip, serve
  it, and run something that opens the TUI.
- **Workaround:** none here (we don't edit reva-fork's output); the
  2026.1102.0 zips, built before #83, work.
- **Suggested fix:** stamp only `import`/`new Worker`/`fetch` URLs (e.g.
  match `from "./x.js"`, `import("./x.js")`, `new URL("./x.js"`), not
  every quoted `./x.js` string; or exclude the imports-object key in
  `reva_ui_web.js`. A web gate that opens the TUI (reva-fork's own, or
  this repository's check-web) would catch it.

## CoSy-side issues (not for reva-fork)

These are in Bob's sources or data and are left as they are:

- **Old examples:** the `examples` text in `CoSy.csy` uses `^+` and
  `i^`, and `tstScript` uses `^eval`. These words are not in the current
  sources.
- **ForthDay15.csy:** its `script0` uses `"m`, which no longer exists, so
  restoring it prints `unknown word: "m` (harmless).
- **SaveRestoreMeta.f:** it is not loaded by CoSy.f, and loading it fails
  on `m@`.
- **Tui.f on its own:** its first line runs `type` on an empty stack, so
  `include Tui.f` outside CoSy.f faults in `type`.

## Fixed in this repository (2026-10-26)

- **CoSy's `caught` (util.f):** it printed any throw code missing from its
  `throwCodes` list as a z-string, so a failed `needs` (code -4) faulted at
  `0xfffffffc` in `Zcount` instead of reporting. It now prints codes
  below 4096 as numbers and other values as strings.
- **`??` / `CShelpFul` (Derived.f):** these searched `./CoSy/*.f`,
  `./src/reva.f` and `./lib/...` as laid out on Bob's machine, so they
  found nothing. `(cosysrc)` now maps those paths to the flat package and
  to reva-fork's `/reva/` tree, on the CLI and in the browser.

#!/bin/sh
# make-web-zip.sh: build the browser REPL as a static site and zip it, ready
# to upload to any web host, unzip, and serve as plain files.
#
#   scripts/make-web-zip.sh [options]          (from anywhere; POSIX sh)
#
#   --package DIR   include DIR (a folder with reva-package.json) as pkg/ and
#                   open it by default; its manifest must list its "files"
#   --name NAME     zip and folder name (default: reva, or the package's id)
#   --version V     version in the name (default: the workspace version)
#   --canvas MODE   default graphics placement: split (default), pane, window
#   --out DIR       where the zip goes (default: target/web)
#   --no-build      use the reva.wasm already in components/web/crates/reva-web/www
#
# Result: OUT/NAME-web-V.zip holding one folder NAME-web-V/ (the site) and
# the same tree unzipped at OUT/NAME-web-V/ (what reva-serve embeds).
#
# The site is static and relative: index.html, the JS modules, reva.wasm,
# canvas.html and, with a package, pkg/.  It needs no server logic, no
# special headers (no SharedArrayBuffer, so no COOP/COEP), and works under
# any subpath (https://host/some/dir/NAME-web-V/).  Files written by Forth
# are kept in the visitor's localStorage, which is per origin: a site moved
# to another host or port starts with no saved files.
#
# The zip is reproducible: files are listed in sorted order and stamped
# with the last commit's time (UTC), so the same commit gives the same zip.
set -eu
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd "$HERE/.." && pwd)
WWW=$ROOT/components/web/crates/reva-web/www
PKG= NAME= VERSION= CANVAS=split OUT=$ROOT/target/web BUILD=1

die() { echo "make-web-zip: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case $1 in
        --package) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "$1 needs a value"; PKG=$2; shift 2 ;;
        --name) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "$1 needs a value"; NAME=$2; shift 2 ;;
        --version) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "$1 needs a value"; VERSION=$2; shift 2 ;;
        --canvas) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "$1 needs a value"; CANVAS=$2; shift 2 ;;
        --out) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "$1 needs a value"; OUT=$2; shift 2 ;;
        --no-build) BUILD=; shift ;;
        -h|--help) sed -n '2,25p' "$0" | cut -c3-; exit 0 ;;
        *) die "unknown option $1 (try --help)" ;;
    esac
done
case $CANVAS in split|pane|window) ;; *) die "--canvas $CANVAS: use split, pane or window" ;; esac
command -v zip >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "needs zip (macOS has it; Debian/Ubuntu: apt install zip)"

if [ -n "$PKG" ]; then
    [ -f "$PKG/reva-package.json" ] || die "$PKG: no reva-package.json"
    PKG=$(cd "$PKG" && pwd)
    grep -q '"files"' "$PKG/reva-package.json" \
        || die "$PKG/reva-package.json has no \"files\" list (a static server cannot list a folder)"
    if [ -z "$NAME" ]; then
        # the manifest's "id", else the folder name
        NAME=$(tr -d '\n' < "$PKG/reva-package.json" | awk '{ if (match($0, /"id"[ \t]*:[ \t]*"[A-Za-z0-9._-]+"/)) { s = substr($0, RSTART, RLENGTH); sub(/.*"id"[ \t]*:[ \t]*"/, "", s); sub(/"$/, "", s); print s } }')
        [ -n "$NAME" ] || NAME=$(basename "$PKG")
    fi
fi
NAME=${NAME:-reva}
case $NAME in *[!A-Za-z0-9._-]*|'') die "--name $NAME: use letters, digits, . _ -" ;; esac
if [ -z "$VERSION" ]; then
    VERSION=$(tr -d ' \n' < "$ROOT/VERSION")
fi

[ -n "$BUILD" ] && "$HERE/build-web.sh" >/dev/null
[ -f "$WWW/reva.wasm" ] || die "no $WWW/reva.wasm (run without --no-build)"

SITE=$NAME-web-$VERSION
mkdir -p "$OUT"
OUT=$(cd "$OUT" && pwd)
STAGE=$OUT/$SITE
ZIP=$OUT/$SITE.zip
rm -rf "$STAGE" "$ZIP"
mkdir -p "$STAGE"
for f in index.html host.js reva.js reva-worker.js reva.wasm ui.js tui.js canvas.html split.js package.js about.js lineedit.js ansi.js sqlite.js store.js upload.js favicon.png favicon.ico; do
    cp "$WWW/$f" "$STAGE/$f"
done
cp -R "$WWW/ui" "$STAGE/ui"
cp "$ROOT/LICENSE" "$STAGE/LICENSE.txt"
cp "$ROOT/LICENSE-MIT" "$STAGE/LICENSE-MIT.txt"

# The page's defaults and the build stamp (About), as meta tags (index.html reads them when the URL
# has no ?package= or ?canvas=).
pkgmeta=
if [ -n "$PKG" ]; then
    mkdir -p "$STAGE/pkg"
    # every file of the package except dot files (.git and friends)
    (cd "$PKG" && find . -type f ! -path '*/.*' | while IFS= read -r f; do
        mkdir -p "$STAGE/pkg/$(dirname "$f")"
        cp "$f" "$STAGE/pkg/$f"
    done)
    pkgmeta=pkg/
fi
# A hash of the site's files (package included): a new build is new module
# URLs below, so browsers never mix stale modules with fresh ones, while an
# unchanged build stays cached.  The page fetches its other files with
# no-cache (reva.js FRESH).  POSIX cksum, files in a fixed order.
site=$(cd "$STAGE" && find . -type f | LC_ALL=C sort | xargs cat | cksum | cut -d' ' -f1)
build="$("$HERE/build-stamp.sh") $site"
awk -v pkg="$pkgmeta" -v canvas="$CANVAS" -v build="$build" '
    index($0, "<meta name=\"reva-package\" content=\"\">") { sub(/content=""/, "content=\"" pkg "\"") }
    index($0, "<meta name=\"reva-canvas\" content=\"\">") { sub(/content=""/, "content=\"" canvas "\"") }
    index($0, "<meta name=\"reva-build\" content=\"\">") { sub(/content=""/, "content=\"" build "\"") }
    { print }' "$WWW/index.html" > "$STAGE/index.html"
grep -q "name=\"reva-canvas\" content=\"$CANVAS\"" "$STAGE/index.html" \
    || die "index.html has no reva-canvas meta tag to set"
# Every module and worker URL ("./x.js"), and the UI's wasm, carry ?v=SITE.
for f in "$STAGE"/*.js "$STAGE"/ui/*.js "$STAGE/index.html"; do
    sed-rs -i -e "s#(\"\\./[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\\.js)\"#\\1?v=$site\"#g" \
        -e "s#'(reva_ui_web_bg\\.wasm)'#'\\1?v=$site'#g" "$f" || die "$f: could not stamp module URLs"
done
grep -q "\"./reva.js?v=$site\"" "$STAGE/index.html" || die "index.html: module URLs not stamped"

cat > "$STAGE/README.txt" <<EOF
$SITE: Reva Forth in the browser (WebAssembly), as a static site.

Serve this folder with any static web server and open index.html:

  - on a web host: upload the zip, unzip it anywhere (a subfolder is fine),
    and open https://your.host/path/$SITE/
  - locally: python3 -m http.server -d $SITE 8000, then http://localhost:8000/
    (or run the reva-serve binary, which embeds the same files)

Opening index.html as a file:// URL does not work: browsers do not run
Web Workers or fetch files from file:// pages.

Files you write in Forth are kept in your browser's localStorage for this
site's origin (scheme, host and port): another host or port starts empty.

URL options: ?canvas=split|pane|window, ?package=DIR/ (another package
folder on the same site), ?include=FILE, ?eval=TEXT, ?image=FILE.

Licenses: LICENSE.txt (Reva, public domain), LICENSE-MIT.txt (the portable
core).$( [ -n "$PKG" ] && printf '\nThe package in pkg/ has its own terms; see its files.' )
EOF

# Reproducible: fixed timestamps (the last commit's, in UTC) and sorted names.
# A package's newest file wins when it is newer: a package rebuilt at the
# same reva-fork commit must still get newer times, or a server that answers
# by Last-Modified (python3 -m http.server) keeps sending the old index.html.
stamp=$(cd "$ROOT" && TZ=UTC git log -1 --format=%cd --date=format-local:%Y%m%d%H%M 2>/dev/null || true)
stamp=${stamp:-202601010000}
find "$STAGE" -exec env TZ=UTC touch -t "$stamp" {} +
if [ -n "$PKG" ]; then
    newest=$(find "$PKG" -type f ! -path '*/.*' -newer "$STAGE/index.html" -exec ls -t {} + | head -1)
    [ -n "$newest" ] && find "$STAGE" -exec touch -r "$newest" {} +
fi
(cd "$OUT" && find "$SITE" | LC_ALL=C sort | TZ=UTC zip -qX -@ "$ZIP")

n=$(find "$STAGE" -type f | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
size=$(wc -c < "$ZIP" | tr -d ' ')
echo "make-web-zip: $ZIP ($n files, $size bytes)"
echo "make-web-zip: site at $STAGE (try: python3 -m http.server -d $STAGE 8000)"

content.text: <total_tokens>14990335 tokens left</total_tokens>

Ask 20 is fixed, and the PR should be up in about 15 minutes, once the full gate passes.

**The cause** was my bug in #83. The web zip build stamped every quoted `"./x.js"`, and in the TUI's generated glue code one of those strings is the name the wasm imports, not a URL. Stamped, the name no longer matched, so the TUI's wasm failed to load.

**The fix:**
- `make-web-zip.sh` now stamps only real URLs: `from "./x.js"`, `import("./x.js")`, `new URL("./x.js"`, and the TUI's wasm URL.
- The script now fails the build if that import name is ever changed again.
- I built a zip and served it the way `python3 -m http.server` does. The notebook opens in the TUI, with no load error.

**The live demo is affected too.** 2026.1103.0 was published with the bad stamping, so the notebook and every TUI fail there now. A new release fixes it; today it would be 2026.1104.0. After you merge the PR, shall I bump `VERSION` and publish?

content.content:
is retired in the three steps set out in [DEPRECATED.md](DEPRECATED.md):
deprecate (done), move to `legacy/www/` once `docs/parity.md` shows every
still-supported topic rebuilt, then delete with the rest of `legacy/`.

## Status

- **Works:** all of `reva.f`; the REPL; `include` and `needs`; contexts;
  the embedded assembler; the file words (real files on the CLI; in the
  browser, in memory and kept in IndexedDB, plus an Upload button);
  `time&date`, `ms@`,
  `getenv`; saved images (`save`, `--image`, also in the browser) and
  `restart`. 69 of the 132
  programs in `examples/` run unchanged
  ([generated report](docs/parity-examples.md)).
- **Hosts:** the `reva` command on any 64-bit platform Rust supports, and a
  zero-import WebAssembly module with a minimal web console that runs it in
  a Web Worker (the page never freezes; Stop interrupts a running word).
- **x87 floating point** with double-precision registers:
  `lib/math/floats` passes its own tests.
- **Not yet:** native C libraries, and translation to native code.

## Roadmap

1. Virtual libraries (Rust bindings inside the VM; no generic native FFI,
   see [docs/portability.md](docs/portability.md)): SQLite, then a UI
   service (panes, keys, SVG, later WebGL 3D) for the browser and the
   desktop app.
2. Translators that turn hot vx86 code into x86-64, ARM64 and WebAssembly,
   to recover native speed (the interpreter is the reference semantics; the
   translations are caches over it).

The first practical goal on this road is a **static WebAssembly demo of
[CoSy](http://cosy.com/)**, Bob Armstrong's APL/K-like vocabulary built on
Reva: a directory of HTML, JavaScript, CSS and a `.wasm` file that can be
served from any static web server, with no installation. The steps above
that it needs (files, then floats) come first; CoSy-specific code is kept
out of this repository, which receives only general-purpose Reva changes.

## Quality

The port is developed with these qualities in mind, each with a concrete
mechanism described in [docs/design.md §4](docs/design.md#4-non-functional-requirements):

- **Portability and availability:** pure Rust, no `unsafe` in the VM, no
  runtime dependencies; one core for the CLI and the browser.
- **Reliability:** bounds-checked memory, stack checks between words, and
  faults that recover to the REPL and roll back a half-made definition.
- **Traceability and serviceability:** faults name the Forth word and
  offset; `reva --trace` logs every step; a probe tool disassembles words.
- **Maintainability and understandability:** `reva.f` is run verbatim, not
  forked; small modules with literate headers; documented deviations.
- **Testability:** unit and API tests (`cargo test`), a golden-output
  regression suite (`scripts/regress.sh`, using
  [reg-rs](https://github.com/sw-cli-tools/reg-rs)), and executed
  documentation samples.
- **Upgradability:** images hold only vx86 bytes and are versioned; native
  translations are never persisted.

## Branches

- `dev`: the default branch. Every change merges here first.
- feature branches: one per change, branched from `dev` and merged back.
- `main`: the tested release line. `dev` merges into `main` (with a merge
  commit, never a squash, so the two histories stay aligned) once the gates
  pass: `cargo test --release --workspace`, `scripts/doc-check.sh` and the
  reg-rs suite. The original x86 import is the first commit, `edc8cbe`.

## Third-party software

- **SQLite** ([public domain](https://sqlite.org/copyright.html)), for
  `needs db/sqlite`. The CLI and the desktop app build it in through the
  [rusqlite](https://github.com/rusqlite/rusqlite) crate (MIT). The browser
  build does not include it: the page loads SQLite's official WebAssembly
  build, the [@sqlite.org/sqlite-wasm](https://github.com/sqlite/sqlite-wasm)
  package (Apache-2.0), from jsDelivr at run time, the first time a program
  uses SQLite.
- The desktop app is built on [Tauri](https://tauri.app) (MIT/Apache-2.0).

Every crate and its license, and what is loaded at run time, are listed in
[docs/licenses.md](docs/licenses.md); the About dialog in the web REPL and
the desktop app credits them too.

## Status

- **Works:** all of `reva.f`; the REPL; `include` and `needs`; contexts;
  the embedded assembler; the file words (real files on the CLI; in the
  browser, in memory and kept in IndexedDB, plus an Upload button);

- **Hosts:** the `reva` command on any 64-bit platform Rust supports, and a
  zero-import WebAssembly module with a minimal web console that runs it in
  a Web Worker (the page never freezes; Stop interrupts a running word).
- **x87 floating point** with double-precision registers:
  `lib/math/floats` passes its own tests.
- **Not yet:** native C libraries, and translation to native code.

## Roadmap

1. Virtual libraries (Rust bindings inside the VM; no generic native FFI,
   see [docs/portability.md](docs/portability.md)): SQLite, then a UI
   service (panes, keys, SVG, later WebGL 3D) for the browser and the
   desktop app.
2. Translators that turn hot vx86 code into x86-64, ARM64 and WebAssembly,
   to recover native speed (the interpreter is the reference semantics; the
   translations are caches over it).

The first practical goal on this road is a **static WebAssembly demo of
[CoSy](http://cosy.com/)**, Bob Armstrong's APL/K-like vocabulary built on
Reva: a directory of HTML, JavaScript, CSS and a `.wasm` file that can be
served from any static web server, with no installation. The steps above
that it needs (files, then floats) come first; CoSy-specific code is kept
out of this repository, which receives only general-purpose Reva changes.

## Quality

The port is developed with these qualities in mind, each with a concrete
mechanism described in [docs/design.md §4](docs/design.md#4-non-functional-requirements):

- **Portability and availability:** pure Rust, no `unsafe` in the VM, no
  runtime dependencies; one core for the CLI and the browser.
- **Reliability:** bounds-checked memory, stack checks between words, and
  faults that recover to the REPL and roll back a half-made definition.
- **Traceability and serviceability:** faults name the Forth word and
  offset; `reva --trace` logs every step; a probe tool disassembles words.
- **Maintainability and understandability:** `reva.f` is run verbatim, not
  forked; small modules with literate headers; documented deviations.
- **Testability:** unit and API tests (`cargo test`), a golden-output
  regression suite (`scripts/regress.sh`, using
  [reg-rs](https://github.com/sw-cli-tools/reg-rs)), and executed
  documentation samples.
- **Upgradability:** images hold only vx86 bytes and are versioned; native
  translations are never persisted.

- `dev`: the default branch. Every change merges here first.
- feature branches: one per change, branched from `dev` and merged back.
- `main`: the tested release line. `dev` merges into `main` (with a merge
